   await expect(bufferRecordingPreparedDownload(file, new AbortController().signal)).rejects.toThrow('256 MiB');\n        const controller = new AbortController();\n        controller.abort();\n        await expect(bufferRecordingPreparedDownload(new Blob(['media']), controller.signal)).rejects.toThrow();\n        expect(read).not.toHaveBeenCalled();\n    });\n\n    it('retains distinct individual source filenames after storage clones their objects', () => {\n        const recording = createTestStudioRecording();\n        for (const track of recording.tracks) {\n            expect(recordingOriginalFilename(structuredClone(recording), track)).toBe(recordingOriginalFilename(recording, track));\n            expect(recordingPreparedFilename(structuredClone(recording), track)).toBe(recordingPreparedFilename(recording, track));\n        }\n        expect(new Set(recording.tracks.map((track) => recordingOriginalFilename(structuredClone(recording), track))).size).toBe(recording.tracks.length);\n        expect(() => recordingPreparedFilename(recording, { ...recording.tracks[0], id: 'absent' })).toThrow();\n    });\n    beforeEach(() => { DOWNLOADS.download.mockReset(); DOWNLOADS.read.mockReset().mockResolvedValue(new Blob(['original bytes'])); });\n    it('downloads source-specific original metadata with an individual source', async base.tracks[0].id, sourceLabel: base.tracks[0].label, mediaRevision: 'a'.repeat(64),\n                createdAt: '2026-09-29T08:00:00.000Z', language: 'cs', processor: 'openai-whisper-1', settings: {} },\n            cues: [{ id: 'cue-one', startSeconds: 1, endSeconds: 2, text: 'Ahoj', isEnabled: true, origin: 'manual' }] };\n        const recording = { ...base, tracks: base.tracks.map((track) => ({ ...track, byteLength: 14, chunkCount: 1 })), derivedTracks: [subtitleTrack] };\n        await exportRecordingOriginal(recording, recording.tracks[0], null, new AbortController().signal);\n        expect(DOWNLOADS.download.mock.calls.map(([download]) => download.fileName)).toEqual([\n            recordingOriginalFilename(recording, recording.tracks[0]),\n            expect.stringMatching(/subtitle-one\\.srt$/), expect.stringMatching(/subtitle-one\\.vtt$/), expect.stringMatching(/subtitle-one\\.json$/),\n        ]);\n    });\n    it('does not claim prepared const reader = new ZipReader(new BlobReader(DOWNLOADS.download.mock.calls[0][0].blob));\n        const entries = await reader.getEntries();\n        expect(entries.map((entry) => if (entry.directory) throw new Error('Expected file');\n            expect(await entry.getData(new TextWriter())).toBe('original bytes');\n        }\n        const manifestEntry = entries[2];\n        if (manifestEntry.directory) throw new Error('Expected manifest');\n        const manifest = JSON.parse(await manifestEntry.getData(new TextWriter())) as RecordingArchiveManifest;\n        expect(manifest.trim).toEqual({ startSeconds: 1, endSeconds: 4 });\n        expect(manifest.isTrimIncluded).toBe(false);\n        expect(manifest.tracks[1].startOffsetSeconds).toBe(0.002);\n        await reader.close();\n    });\n    it('aborts a disk destination when the export is cancelled instead of closing a partial archive', async () => {\n        const abort = vi.fn();\n        const close it('retains distinct individual source filenames after storage clones their objects', () => {\n        const recording = createTestStudioRecording();\n        for (const track of recording.tracks) {\n expect(recordingPreparedFilename(structuredClone(recording), track)).toBe(recordingPreparedFilename(recording, track));\n        }\n        expect(new Set(recording.tracks.map((track) => OPFS here replaces only the OS picker; this does NOT test quota bypass.\n        value: async () => (await navigator.storage.getDirectory()).getDirectoryHandle('studio-directory-test', { create: true }),\n    }));\n    await openStudio(page, baseURL);\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Vybrat složku pro nahrávání' }).click();\n    await expect(page.getByRole('region', { name: 'Úložiště záznamu' })).toContainText('Složka studio-directory-test');\n    await addSource(page, 'camera'); await addSource(page, 'screen'); await addSource(page, 'microphone');\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Nahrávat připravené zdroje', exact: true }).click();\n    await expect(page.getByTestId('recording-committed-bytes')).not.toHaveText('0 B');\n    // Origin metadata is a cache for this backend: it must not roll back closed directory checkpoints.\n    await page.evaluate(() => {\n        const originalPut = IDBObjectStore.prototype.put;\n        IDBObjectStore.prototype.put = function (value, key) {\n            const request = key === undefined ? originalPut.call(this, value) : originalPut.call(this, value, key);\n            if (this.name === 'recordings') this.transaction.abort();\n            return request;\n        };\n    });\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Zastavit všechny stopy', exact: true }).click();\n    await expect(page.getByText('Uloženo', { exact: true })).toBeVisible();\n    await page.reload();\n    await expect(page.getByText('Uloženo', { exact: true })).toBeVisible();\n    const metadata = await page.evaluate(async () => {\n        const database = await new Promise<IDBDatabase>((resolve) => { const request = indexedDB.open('promptbook-recording-studio'); request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result); });\n        const recordings = await new Promise<import('@/lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioTypes').StudioRecording[]>((resolve) => {\n            const request = database.transaction('recordings').objectStore('recordings').getAll(); request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result);\n        });\n        const chunks = await new Promise<number>((resolve) => { const request = database.transaction('chunks').objectStore('chunks').count(); request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result); });\n        database.close();\n        return { recording: recordings[0], chunks };\n    });\n    expect(metadata.chunks).toBe(0);\n    expect(metadata.recording.tracks.every((track) => track.byteLength > 0)).toBe(true);\n    const download = page.waitForEvent('download');\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Originály ZIP', exact: true }).click();\n    const files = await readArchive((await (await download).path())!);\n    for (const [name, bytes] of Array.from(files)) {\n        if (!name.startsWith('originals/')) continue;\n        const input = new Input({ formats: ALL_FORMATS, source: new BufferSource(bytes) });\n        try { expect(await input.canRead()).toBe(true); expect(await input.computeDuration()).toBeGreaterThan(3); }\n        finally { input.dispose(); }\n    }\n    await page.evaluate(async (recordingId) => {\n        const parent = await (await navigator.storage.getDirectory()).getDirectoryHandle('studio-directory-test');\n        const directory = await parent.getDirectoryHandle(`promptbook-recording-${recordingId}`);\n        Object.defineProperty(window, 'showDirectoryPicker', { configurable: true, value: async () => directory });\n        const database = await new Promise<IDBDatabase>((resolve) => { const request = indexedDB.open('promptbook-recording-studio'); request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result); });\n        await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {\n            const transaction = database.transaction(['recordings', 'directories'], 'readwrite');\n            transaction.objectStore('recordings').clear(); transaction.objectStore('directories').clear();\n            transaction.oncomplete = () => resolve(); transaction.onabort = () => reject(transaction.error);\n        });\n        database.close();\n    }, metadata.recording.id);\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Obnovit záznam ze složky' }).click();\n    await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Obnovit záznam ze složky' })).toBeEnabled();\n    await page.reload();\n    await expect(page.getByText('Uloženo', { exact: true })).toHaveCount(1);\n\n    // A separate visit with no cached handle must recover even if both destinations refuse further writes.\n    await page.evaluate(async () => {\n        const database = await new Promise<IDBDatabase>((resolve) => { const request = indexedDB.open('promptbook-recording-studio'); request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result); });\n        await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {\n            const transaction = database.transaction(['recordings', 'directories'], 'readwrite');\n            transaction.objectStore('recordings').clear(); transaction.objectStore('directories').clear();\n            transaction.oncomplete = () => resolve();\n        });\n        database.close();\n    });\n    await page.reload();\n    await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Obnovit záznam ze složky' })).toBeEnabled();\n    await page.evaluate(async (recordingId) => {\n        const parent = await (await navigator.storage.getDirectory()).getDirectoryHandle('studio-directory-test');\n        const directory = await parent.getDirectoryHandle(`promptbook-recording-${recordingId}`);\n        Object.defineProperty(window, 'showDirectoryPicker', { configurable: true, value: async () => directory });\n        const originalPut = IDBObjectStore.prototype.put;\n        IDBObjectStore.prototype.put = function (value, key) {\n            const request = key === undefined ? originalPut.call(this, value) : originalPut.call(this, value, key);\n            this.transaction.abort();\n            return request;\n        };\n        FileSystemFileHandle.prototype.createWritable = async () => { throw new DOMException('Simulated full disk', 'QuotaExceededError'); };\n    }, metadata.recording.id);\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Obnovit záznam ze složky' }).click();\n    await expect(page.getByText('Uloženo', { exact: true })).toHaveCount(1);\n    const recoveredDownload = page.waitForEvent('download');\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Stáhnout originál 1', exact: true }).click();\n    const firstOriginal = Array.from(files.keys()).find((name) => name.startsWith('originals/01-camera'));\n    expect(firstOriginal).toBeDefined();\n    expect(await readFile((await (await recoveredDownload).path())!)).toEqual(Buffer.from(files.get(firstOriginal!)!));\n});\n\ntest('keeps committed multi-source data after a real IndexedDB transaction abort and offers recovery', async ({ page, baseURL }) => {\n    await openStudio(page, baseURL);\n    await addSource(page, 'camera'); await addSource(page, 'screen');\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Nahrávat připravené zdroje', exact: true }).click();\n    await expect(page.getByTestId('recording-bitrate')).toContainText('/s');\n    await page.evaluate(() => {\n        const originalAdd = IDBObjectStore.prototype.add;\n        IDBObjectStore.prototype.add = function (value, key) {\n            const request = key === undefined ? originalAdd.call(this, value) : originalAdd.call(this, value, key);\n            if (this.name === 'chunks') this.transaction.abort();\n            return request;\n        };\n    });\n    await expect(page.getByText('Přerušený záznam', { exact: true })).toBeVisible();\n    await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Zastavit všechny stopy', exact: true })).toHaveCount(0);\n    await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Originály ZIP', exact: true })).toBeEnabled();\n    await page.reload();\n    await expect(page.getByText('Přerušený záznam', { exact: true })).toBeVisible();\n    const download = page.waitForEvent('download');\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Originály ZIP', exact: true }).click();\n    const files = await readArchive((await (await download).path())!);\n    const manifest = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(files.get('recording.json'))) as RecordingArchiveManifest;\n    expect(manifest.status).toBe('interrupted'); expect(manifest.missingRanges.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);\n    expect(manifest.tracks.every((track) => track.byteLength > 0)).toBe(true);\n});\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":828,"oldLines":7,"newStart":828,"newLines":7,"lines":["     // No original may leave the studio unseekable, however the browser's recorder wrote its container.","     const unseekableOriginals: string[] = [];","     for (const name of originalNames) {","-        const report = await readRecordingIndexReport(new Blob([originals.get(name)!]));","+        const report = await readRecordingIndexReport(new Blob([new Uint8Array(originals.get(name)!)]));","         if (report.status !== 'indexed') unseekableOriginals.push(`${name}: ${report.status} — ${report.detail}`);","     }","     expect(unseekableOriginals).toEqual([]);"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}

The small\n64\twrites do not prove that a recording can exceed 10 GB or that the machine has enough space for a ten-hour take.\n65\t\n66\t## Storage and failure contract\n67\t\n68\t- `Odhad prostoru pro web` reports only current origin headroom. Raw usage/quota and update time are available in\n69\t  the details. There is no physical-disk countdown: **Skutečné volné místo nelze v tomto prohlížeči zjistit**.\n70\t  Stale, invalid, missing, rejected and timed-out estimates become unknown. The fixed-10-GiB explanation is a\n71\t  possibility, not browser detection. Recorded bytes are never subtracted from already usage-adjusted headroom.\n72\t- Committed media bytes come from acknowledged storage checkpoints; queued bytes are distinct. Combined VBR uses\n73\t  all source bytes on the existing session clock over a bounded window. Startup or a stalled/paused input yields\n74\t  no current rate, never infinity. The configured rate includes embedded audio and every selected source.\n75\t  There is currently no pause/resume implementation: the related editor/control prompts are still marked TODO.\n76\t  They must reuse this clock and storage contract, not infer pause timing from capacity telemetry.\n77\t- `navigator.storage.persist()` is invoked only by its explicit button. Granted, denied, unsupported and error\n78\t  states are separate. The existing origin can still be cleared manually or hit a write limit.\n79\t- Browser storage retains the original atomic IndexedDB chunk/counter transactions. A fresh low origin estimate\n80\t  can stop/prevent origin capture with a 64 MiB reserve. A high estimate never guarantees a successful write.\n81\t- Selected-directory capture creates one uniquely named session subfolder. Every normally five-second source\n82\t  fragment is closed, then a small manifest replacement is closed; only then are those bytes acknowledged.\n83\t  No growing-file `keepExistingData` copy and no full-session assembly occurs at finalization. Directory media\n84\t  does not enter IndexedDB/OPFS. The origin still needs space for a small initial metadata/handle registration;\n85\t  later cache-write failure cannot roll back the authoritative directory checkpoint.\n86\t- Import recovery requests read access and does not rewrite the folder checkpoint. It retains readable metadata\n87\t  and the selected handle for the current visit even if origin registration fails, so a full disk/origin cannot\n88\t  block streaming out already committed media. If the browser cannot remember the handle, select that same\n89\t  recording subfolder again next visit. Editing/deletion still require write permission and successful writes;\n90\t  the explicit reconnect action can request that permission. A new studio visit reloads the cache under its lock.\n91\t- File counts grow with duration/source count (about 7,200 parts per source in ten hours at regular five-second\n92\t  delivery). Filesystem latency/antivirus and encoder bursts can therefore matter; this tradeoff favors bounded\n93\t  commits and crash recovery over keeping huge uncommitted writable files open. Actual ten-hour performance is\n94\t  not yet validated. Browser-internal MediaRecorder buffering is outside the application's bound.\n95\t- The application retains at most 64 MiB of pending chunks. Backlog overflow, quota, permission, disk or source\n96\t  failure stops all recorders through the existing barrier and drains earlier queued writes. After a failed chunk,\n97\t  later chunks are not appended beyond a hole. Previously committed prefixes remain available. Final checkpoint\n98\t  failure leaves an interrupted take, never a false success. Recovery uses the last checkpoint even when saving\n99\t  a recovery status in a full origin fails.\n100\t  A source that supplied no media makes the whole take interrupted, even if its recorder reported a normal stop.\n101\t- `captureEndSeconds` and manifest `missingRanges` use source IDs and seconds on the same session timeline.\n102\t  An unclean crash has an unknown tail end (`null`). Common recoverable duration is the last point all sources\n103\t  have committed, and no source is moved left to conceal a gap. Files can still need player/container repair\n104\t  after interruption; the studio does not promise every truncated codec stream will decode.\n105\t- A crash after closing a part but before checkpointing may leave an **unindexed part**. It is preserved in the\n106\t  directory but is not claimed as recoverable timed media. Do not delete it if external repair is needed. Recovery\n107\t  never overwrites media, obtains unrelated permissions, or deletes recordings to reclaim space.\n108\t- ZIP64 reads original chunks serially with backpressure; byte counters are exact JavaScript safe integers, not\n109\t  signed/unsigned 32-bit integers. A ZIP needs destination space for its outputs. A trimmed ZIP adds trimmed\n110\t  outputs plus one temporary trimmed track in OPFS. That temporary space is explicitly disclosed. Individual\n111\t  original downloads use disk-backed Blob references when a native save picker is unavailable; the browser's own\n112\t  large-Blob/media limits still apply. Only the buffered ZIP fallback is capped (256 MiB), not capture size.\n113\t  **Stáhnout údaje o stopách** downloads the same versioned manifest for the separately named original files,\n114\t  keeping offsets, source IDs, trim and missing ranges available without creating a ZIP.\n115\t\n116\t## Validation and remaining hardware work\n117\t\n118\tAutomated suites: `npm test -- lib/recording-studio` and\n119\t`npm run test-e2e -- tests/e2e/recording-studio.spec.ts`. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CfZrcisrB7E3JkFbM2v4y","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01QuwKGjt2VZAsxJHYgCyQfG","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\me\\work\\promptbook-experiments-and-landing-pages\\aldaron\\docs\\recording-studio-seek-index.md","content":"# Recording studio seek index: analysis, contract and verification\n\nThe owner reported that studio recordings \"often result in videos with broken index\" and repaired them by hand:\n\n```bash\nfor f in Zaznam-28-9-2026-12-52-35-316ef072-*.webm; do ffmpeg -i \"$f\" -map 0 -c copy \"${f%.webm}-fixed.webm\"; done\n```\n\nThe filename pattern is `recordingOriginalFilename`/`recordingOriginalPartFilename` in\n`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioExport.ts`, so those were **individually downloaded originals**.\n\n## What was actually broken\n\nNothing in the media. `ffmpeg -map 0 -c copy` re-encodes nothing; it only rewrites the container. What was missing\nis the container's seek metadata, and it was missing by design:\n\n- Capture uses `MediaRecorder` (`lib/recording-studio/RecordingStudioCapture.ts`), started with a timeslice so each\n  chunk can be committed atomically to IndexedDB or to a selected directory.\n- A `MediaRecorder` muxes for streaming. Its Matroska `Segment` element carries an **unknown size**, no `Cues`\n  element is written, and `Info/Duration` is absent, because the browser does not know where the file ends while it\n  is still being written. Safari's fragmented MP4 is the same story without an `mfra`/`sidx` index.\n- `readRecordingPart` concatenates the committed chunks verbatim, so an exported original was exactly those live\n  bytes. Players that scan (including this studio's own mediabunny-based preview) cope; editors that rely on the\n  index cannot seek.\n\nSo this was never an intermittent fault — **every** WebM the studio handed out was unseekable, and \"often\" reflects\nwhich downstream tool noticed.\n\n## Why prevention cannot happen inside the recorder\n\n`MediaRecorder` exposes no option to write an index, and its muxer is not replaceable. The only ways to obtain one\nare to write the container ourselves (WebCodecs plus a muxer, which would give up the browser's proven capture path\nand its Safari fallback) or to rewrite the container after the recorder has closed a part.\n\nRewriting the committed media in place was rejected: an 8 Mbit/s screen share is about 1 MB/s, so a one-hour part is\naround 3.6 GB. Doubling that transiently is not acceptable against the browser's ~10 GiB origin estimate, it would\nadd minutes to **Stop**, and for a selected-directory destination it would have to overwrite the immutable fragments\nthat crash recovery depends on. Committed capture bytes therefore stay untouched.\n\n## What the studio does instead\n\n### One home for the question\n\n`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioIndex.ts` is the only place that decides what a usable index is. It has no\ndependencies: it reads at most 256 KiB of the container head plus 64 KiB of its tail through `Blob.slice`, walks the\nEBML or ISOBMFF element headers, and never touches media bytes.\n\n| Status | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| `indexed` | Matroska with `Cues` (or a `SeekHead` entry pointing at them) **and** a stored `Duration`; or MP4 with a non-zero `mvhd` duration and either sample tables or `mfra`/`sidx` |\n| `unindexed` | A live container: an unknown-size `Segment`, missing `Cues`, or a missing/zero duration |\n| `unknown` | Not Matroska or MP4, empty, or a header that does not fit the read window — never raises an alarm |\n\n`RECORDING_INDEX_REPAIR_COMMAND` and the two message builders live there too, so the recorded reason, the alert and\nthe archive README all say the same thing.\n\n### A check immediately after recording, and the alert\n\n`RecordingStudioCapture.verifyPartIndex` runs as each part closes — at a global pause and at Stop, beside the\nexisting `measurePart` — and stores the verdict on `RecordingMediaPart.indexStatus`.\n\nA part without an index is the ordinary outcome, so it is recorded rather than announced; alerting on every take\nwould make the sound and the browser notification worthless. Two outcomes do reach\n`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioAlerts.ts`, both with the new `recording-kept` impact (warning severity, title\n`… je uložený · potřebuje opravu`):\n\n- the container has no index **and** `canRebuildRecordingIndex` reports that this browser could not build one, so\n  only `ffmpeg` will repair it — the message names the exact command;\n- the container could not be checked at all.\n\n`recording-kept` is announced but deliberately **not** written into the take's `errorMessage`: nothing was lost and\nnothing stopped, so a complete take stays `complete` and remains valid for `Donahrát`. Where the work is needed is\nrecorded on the part it concerns. Rebuild support is probed once per MIME type per take.\n\n### The index is written on the way out\n\n`deliverRecordingOriginal` in `recordingStudioExport.ts` is the single rule for handing over recorded media, used by\nboth the individual original download and the ZIP's `originals/` entries. When the stored part is `unindexed` it\ncalls `withRebuiltRecordingIndex` (`recordingStudioReindex.ts`), which is the browser's own `-map 0 -c copy`:\n\n- `Conversion` with `copy: { mode: 'forced', shiftTolerance: 0 }` — a codec that would need transcoding discards its\n  track instead of silently producing different media, and no timestamp may shift, because the take's session\n  mapping was measured against the recorded ones;\n- output through the shared seekable OPFS working file (`recordingStudioTemporaryFile.ts`, extracted from the trim\n  path so trimming and reindexing share one temporary-file and cleanup implementation);\n- the result is accepted only after it reports `indexed` and its bounds match the part's measured `mediaBounds`\n  within 50 ms with the same component count.\n\nAny failure — unsupported codec, missing OPFS, a rebuilt file over the 256 MiB detached-download limit with no disk\npicker, or failed verification — falls back to the recorder's own bytes and records the reason. Each\n`recording.json` `originalParts` entry carries `status`, `isIndexRebuilt` and that `reason`, and `README.txt`\nexplains both cases and names the ffmpeg command.\n\nPrepared (trimmed) files were already written by mediabunny and always carried an index; nothing about them changed.\n\n## Limits\n\n- Committed capture bytes are never rewritten, so a recording restored from IndexedDB or a selected directory is\n  still a live container until it is exported. The studio's own preview does not need the index.\n- A rebuild costs one full read plus one OPFS-sized write per part, which is why the ZIP and the individual download\n  disclose their temporary-space needs exactly as trimming already did.\n- Unknown containers are reported as `unknown` and handed over untouched. That is not a claim that they are fine.\n- Safari's fragmented MP4 path is implemented against the specification and covered by fixtures, but was not\n  verified on a physical Mac; only Chromium/Edge WebM output was exercised end to end.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `npm test -- lib/recording-studio` — the container parser is covered by deterministic byte fixtures built with the\n  shared encoders in `recordingStudioTestUtilities.ts`: a live Segment with both the eight-byte and Chrome's\n  single-byte unknown size, a remuxed container, `Cues` before the clusters, a missing duration, missing `Cues`, a\n  header outgrowing the read window, foreign bytes, a fragmented MP4 with and without a reachable `mfro`, a plain\n  MP4, and a `moov` past the window. Capture tests cover the recorded verdict per part, the alert for a\n  non-rebuildable index, the alert for an uncheckable container, an already indexed container, and a pause closing\n  two parts. Export tests cover a rebuilt individual download, the fallback with its reason, and the manifest.\n- `npm run test-e2e -- tests/e2e/recording-studio.spec.ts` — with real `MediaRecorder` output, the individually\n  downloaded camera original is asserted to be `unindexed` in storage and `indexed` after download, with the same\n  track count and a duration within 50 ms of the recorded media; every one of the five `originals/` entries in the\n  archive is asserted `indexed` and reported as rebuilt in its manifest.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2225,"cache_read_input_tokens":355733,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2225},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c3f1314a-cae1-41ec-a96d-862a46014ec8","uuid":"08160f4b-143c-4b04-9415-93db2908cd56","timestamp":"2026-09-30T15:25:35.766Z","request_id":"req_011CfZrciM6WzMymMNF6a33n","wire_tool_inputs":{"toolu_01QuwKGjt2VZAsxJHYgCyQfG":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\me\\work\\promptbook-experiments-and-landing-pages\\aldaron\\docs\\recording-studio-seek-index.md","content":"# Recording studio seek index: analysis, contract and verification\n\nThe owner reported that studio recordings \"often result in videos with broken index\" and repaired them by hand:\n\n```bash\nfor f in Zaznam-28-9-2026-12-52-35-316ef072-*.webm; do ffmpeg -i \"$f\" -map 0 -c copy \"${f%.webm}-fixed.webm\"; done\n```\n\nThe filename pattern is `recordingOriginalFilename`/`recordingOriginalPartFilename` in\n`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioExport.ts`, so those were **individually downloaded originals**.\n\n## What was actually broken\n\nNothing in the media. `ffmpeg -map 0 -c copy` re-encodes nothing; it only rewrites the container. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01QuwKGjt2VZAsxJHYgCyQfG","type":"tool_result","content":"File created successfully at: C:\\Users\\me\\work\\promptbook-experiments-and-landing-pages\\aldaron\\docs\\recording-studio-seek-index.md (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c3f1314a-cae1-41ec-a96d-862a46014ec8","uuid":"1343d2c9-dedb-4453-aee2-f1c82ecd5516","timestamp":"2026-09-30T15:25:35.802Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"create","filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\work\\promptbook-experiments-and-landing-pages\\aldaron\\docs\\recording-studio-seek-index.md","content":"# Recording studio seek index: analysis, contract and verification\n\nThe owner reported that studio recordings \"often result in videos with broken index\" and repaired them by hand:\n\n```bash\nfor f in Zaznam-28-9-2026-12-52-35-316ef072-*.webm; do ffmpeg -i \"$f\" -map 0 -c copy \"${f%.webm}-fixed.webm\"; done\n```\n\nThe filename pattern is `recordingOriginalFilename`/`recordingOriginalPartFilename` in\n`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioExport.ts`, so those were **individually downloaded originals**.\n\n## What was actually broken\n\nNothing in the media. `ffmpeg -map 0 -c copy` re-encodes nothing; it only rewrites the container. What was missing\nis the container's seek metadata, and it was missing by design:\n\n- Capture uses `MediaRecorder` (`lib/recording-studio/RecordingStudioCapture.ts`), started with a timeslice so each\n  chunk can be committed atomically to IndexedDB or to a selected directory.\n- A `MediaRecorder` muxes for streaming. Its Matroska `Segment` element carries an **unknown size**, no `Cues`\n  element is written, and `Info/Duration` is absent, because the browser does not know where the file ends while it\n  is still being written. Safari's fragmented MP4 is the same story without an `mfra`/`sidx` index.\n- `readRecordingPart` concatenates the committed chunks verbatim, so an exported original was exactly those live\n  bytes. Players that scan (including this studio's own mediabunny-based preview) cope; editors that rely on the\n  index cannot seek.\n\nSo this was never an intermittent fault — **every** WebM the studio handed out was unseekable, and \"often\" reflects\nwhich downstream tool noticed.\n\n## Why prevention cannot happen inside the recorder\n\n`MediaRecorder` exposes no option to write an index, and its muxer is not replaceable. The only ways to obtain one\nare to write the container ourselves (WebCodecs plus a muxer, which would give up the browser's proven capture path\nand its Safari fallback) or to rewrite the container after the recorder has closed a part.\n\nRewriting the committed media in place was rejected: an 8 Mbit/s screen share is about 1 MB/s, so a one-hour part is\naround 3.6 GB. Doubling that transiently is not acceptable against the browser's ~10 GiB origin estimate, it would\nadd minutes to **Stop**, and for a selected-directory destination it would have to overwrite the immutable fragments\nthat crash recovery depends on. Committed capture bytes therefore stay untouched.\n\n## What the studio does instead\n\n### One home for the question\n\n`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioIndex.ts` is the only place that decides what a usable index is. It has no\ndependencies: it reads at most 256 KiB of the container head plus 64 KiB of its tail through `Blob.slice`, walks the\nEBML or ISOBMFF element headers, and never touches media bytes.\n\n| Status | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| `indexed` | Matroska with `Cues` (or a `SeekHead` entry pointing at them) **and** a stored `Duration`; or MP4 with a non-zero `mvhd` duration and either sample tables or `mfra`/`sidx` |\n| `unindexed` | A live container: an unknown-size `Segment`, missing `Cues`, or a missing/zero duration |\n| `unknown` | Not Matroska or MP4, empty, or a header that does not fit the read window — never raises an alarm |\n\n`RECORDING_INDEX_REPAIR_COMMAND` and the two message builders live there too, so the recorded reason, the alert and\nthe archive README all say the same thing.\n\n### A check immediately after recording, and the alert\n\n`RecordingStudioCapture.verifyPartIndex` runs as each part closes — at a global pause and at Stop, beside the\nexisting `measurePart` — and stores the verdict on `RecordingMediaPart.indexStatus`.\n\nA part without an index is the ordinary outcome, so it is recorded rather than announced; alerting on every take\nwould make the sound and the browser notification worthless. Two outcomes do reach\n`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioAlerts.ts`, both with the new `recording-kept` impact (warning severity, title\n`… je uložený · potřebuje opravu`):\n\n- the container has no index **and** `canRebuildRecordingIndex` reports that this browser could not build one, so\n  only `ffmpeg` will repair it — the message names the exact command;\n- the container could not be checked at all.\n\n`recording-kept` is announced but deliberately **not** written into the take's `errorMessage`: nothing was lost and\nnothing stopped, so a complete take stays `complete` and remains valid for `Donahrát`. Where the work is needed is\nrecorded on the part it concerns. Rebuild support is probed once per MIME type per take.\n\n### The index is written on the way out\n\n`deliverRecordingOriginal` in `recordingStudioExport.ts` is the single rule for handing over recorded media, used by\nboth the individual original download and the ZIP's `originals/` entries. When the stored part is `unindexed` it\ncalls `withRebuiltRecordingIndex` (`recordingStudioReindex.ts`), which is the browser's own `-map 0 -c copy`:\n\n- `Conversion` with `copy: { mode: 'forced', shiftTolerance: 0 }` — a codec that would need transcoding discards its\n  track instead of silently producing different media, and no timestamp may shift, because the take's session\n  mapping was measured against the recorded ones;\n- output through the shared seekable OPFS working file (`recordingStudioTemporaryFile.ts`, extracted from the trim\n  path so trimming and reindexing share one temporary-file and cleanup implementation);\n- the result is accepted only after it reports `indexed` and its bounds match the part's measured `mediaBounds`\n  within 50 ms with the same component count.\n\nAny failure — unsupported codec, missing OPFS, a rebuilt file over the 256 MiB detached-download limit with no disk\npicker, or failed verification — falls back to the recorder's own bytes and records the reason. Each\n`recording.json` `originalParts` entry carries `status`, `isIndexRebuilt` and that `reason`, and `README.txt`\nexplains both cases and names the ffmpeg command.\n\nPrepared (trimmed) files were already written by mediabunny and always carried an index; nothing about them changed.\n\n## Limits\n\n- Committed capture bytes are never rewritten, so a recording restored from IndexedDB or a selected directory is\n  still a live container until it is exported. The studio's own preview does not need the index.\n- A rebuild costs one full read plus one OPFS-sized write per part, which is why the ZIP and the individual download\n  disclose their temporary-space needs exactly as trimming already did.\n- Unknown containers are reported as `unknown` and handed over untouched. That is not a claim that they are fine.\n- Safari's fragmented MP4 path is implemented against the specification and covered by fixtures, but was not\n  verified on a physical Mac; only Chromium/Edge WebM output was exercised end to end.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `npm test -- lib/recording-studio` — the container parser is covered by deterministic byte fixtures built with the\n  shared encoders in `recordingStudioTestUtilities.ts`: a live Segment with both the eight-byte and Chrome's\n  single-byte unknown size, a remuxed container, `Cues` before the clusters, a missing duration, missing `Cues`, a\n  header outgrowing the read window, foreign bytes, a fragmented MP4 with and without a reachable `mfro`, a plain\n  MP4, and a `moov` past the window. Capture tests cover the recorded verdict per part, the alert for a\n  non-rebuildable index, the alert for an uncheckable container, an already indexed container, and a pause closing\n  two parts. Export tests cover a rebuilt individual download, the fallback with its reason, and the manifest.\n- `npm run test-e2e -- tests/e2e/recording-studio.spec.ts` — with real `MediaRecorder` output, the individually\n  downloaded camera original is asserted to be `unindexed` in storage and `indexed` after download, with the same\n  track count and a duration within 50 ms of the recorded media; every one of the five `originals/` entries in the\n  archive is asserted `indexed` and reported as rebuilt in its manifest.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01XXsd6Sgu7rKcRYExNwE79Q","type":"tool_result","content":"214\t  deliberately reconnected, and each display source opens the browser chooser again. Readiness must be checked\n215\t  before Start and follows required microphone mute/unmute events; cancellation or a missing device keeps its source\n216\t  configuration and never substitutes another device silently. One capture coordinator starts and stops sources on a\n217\t  shared clock; a lost source stops only its own track and leaves the rest of the session in it as a gap, while the\n218\t  remaining sources record on. The take ends when no source is left to record or when the shared storage fails, and\n219\t  it is saved as interrupted naming every source it lost. A muted required video track is temporarily\n220\t  unavailable, blocks Start, and takes its own track out of an active take rather than acting like an intentional pause;\n221\t  reselect the source to reconnect. Every failure passes through one channel in `recordingStudioAlerts.ts`, which\n222\t  shows it on the source card and the page, plays a synthesized sound and posts a browser notification, because the\n223\t  administrator is normally working in the application being recorded rather than watching the studio tab. Both\n224\t  channels are on by default, are turned off separately in browser-local settings, and an explicit test button raises\n225\t  a real alert through the real channels. A refused or missing channel leaves the others announcing.\n226\t  The display-source picker belongs to the browser/OS: `displaySurface` is a type\n227\t  preference, the app does not enumerate system windows, and saved names cannot force a window or restore its stream.\n228\t  The macOS Spaces help is shown for manually selected, restored, and reused display configurations. It scopes the\n229\t  reported cross-Space behavior to the owner's unspecified Mac/Chrome versions and links to an authenticated plain\n230\t  `getDisplayMedia({ video: true, audio: false })` diagnostic at `/admin/recording-studio/capture-probe`. Whole-display\n231\t  capture remains an explicit user choice with a privacy warning, never an automatic fallback. Native picker behavior\n232\t  and capture continuity across Spaces require physical Mac testing; mocked browser tests do not establish them.\n233\t  IndexedDB commits each chunk together with its counters; a feature-detected selected-directory destination\n234\t  closes immutable media fragments before its small authoritative checkpoint and stores only handles/metadata in\n235\t  IndexedDB. Recovery can reconnect or import that folder without moving its media into origin storage; read-only\n236\t  import still offers export when further folder or origin-cache writes fail. An exclusive\n237\t  browser lock protects recording, recovery, editing and deletion across tabs. Committed bytes, queued bytes,\n238\t  destination and aggregate bitrate are separate from the browser's labelled origin quota estimate. That estimate\n239\t  can remain constant at 10 GiB, is never physical disk capacity, and supplies no remaining-time countdown.\n240\t  Explicit persistence reports the browser's real result and protects against eviction only. A bounded write queue\n241\t  and all-source failure stop preserve committed prefixes and identify missing tails on the shared session clock.\n242\t  Saved takes survive reload; unfinished ones expose only\n243\t  persisted chunks. Each take retains an immutable snapshot of its intended source configuration. Its editor and list\n244\t  can load that snapshot as a new browser-local setup; a changed setup is replaced only after confirmation, matching\n245\t  live captures may stay connected, and every other source still needs its ordinary per-source readiness action.\n246\t  Screen/window labels are hints only and always go through the browser chooser again. Older takes reconstruct only\n247\t  their stored track details and leave unknown camera/microphone identities for the administrator to select.\n248\t  Reusing settings never starts recording or changes the old take. Saved recordings open the authenticated\n249\t  `/admin/recording-studio/<recordingId>` workspace, sharing the setup/recording shell and its browser lock. Existing\n250\t  IDs and original media stay unchanged; a URL identifies local data and missing local media remains explicit.\n251\t  One transport, playhead and zoomable timeline map source offsets/segments onto session time, wait for asynchronous\n252\t  seeks/buffering and playback starts, correct drift, and hide unavailable frames. Pausing or revealing a hidden\n253\t  video settles its decoded frame even if its clock was already correct. The target after settling is 100 ms, not\n254\t  hardware synchronization. Video visibility/solo and audio mute/solo are separate monitoring choices; one audio\n255\t  source is audible initially and every source remains in export. Shared IN/OUT handles and precise seconds edit\n256\t  one non-destructive selection with undo/reset and the existing autosave/error/navigation protection.\n257\t  ZIP64 exports stream original chunks and a versioned recipe/manifest with explicit seconds, segment mappings,\n258\t  selected interval, prepared zero, missing ranges and per-source processing. Prepared files retain each source's\n259\t  audio; video uses its recorded nominal frame rate when known, with resampling recorded in the manifest.\n260\t  Files are transcoded and checked within 50 ms of the common boundaries; unsupported or discontinuous sources\n261\t  remain clearly labelled originals plus recipe. Trimming uses browser codecs and one temporary local file, never\n262\t  an upload or a composed layout. Individual prepared files have JSON sidecars; cancel/retry preserves originals.\n263\t  Prepared downloads without a disk picker are detached before temporary-file cleanup and limited to 256 MiB;\n264\t  larger prepared files need a disk stream. Individual originals are downloadable when a large ZIP cannot stream\n265\t  to disk; export and OPFS temporary-space needs are disclosed. Capture and export reuse admin navigation/sign-out/reload protection. No server or\n266\t  database storage is added.\n267\t  The same workspace offers a responsive live monitor with grid, focus and pinned-source layouts; hidden or\n268\t  minimized previews, preview sound and camera mirror preferences are browser-local presentation settings and never\n269\t  alter armed recorder sources or raw files.
