'unknown', isIndexRebuilt: false, reason: report?.detail };\n    }\n    const { withRebuiltRecordingIndex, RecordingIndexRebuildUnavailable } = await import('./recordingStudioReindex');","originalFile":"import { BlobReader, BlobWriter, TextReader, ZipWriter } from '@zip.js/zip.js';\nimport { downloadBlobFile } from '@/lib/downloadBlobFile';\nimport { readRecordingPart, readRecordingTrack, streamRecordingPart, streamRecordingTrack } from './recordingStudioStorage';\nimport { addRecordingBytes, getRecordingByteLength, getRecordingMissingRanges, validateRecordingTrim } from './recordingStudioTiming';\nimport { readRecordingIndexReport, RECORDING_INDEX_REPAIR_COMMAND } from './recordingStudioIndex';\nimport type { RecordingArchiveIndexState, RecordingArchiveManifest, RecordingArchiveTrack, RecordingMediaPart, RecordingTrack, StudioRecording } from './recordingStudioTypes';\nimport { createRecordingEditRecipe, getRecordingMediaParts, getRecordingPartForSelection, getRecordingPartTrack, getRecordingSessionDuration, getRecordingUnavailableRanges } from './recordingStudioSessionTime';\nimport { getRecordingDerivedFiles, getRecordingDerivedManifestEntries, type RecordingDerivedFile } from './recordingStudioDerivedExport';\nimport { createRecordingWorkshopSidecar } from './recordingStudioWorkshop';\n\nconst MAXIMUM_BUFFERED_EXPORT_BYTES = 256 * 1024 * 1024;\n\ntype RecordingWorkshopFile = { readonly filename: string; readonly content: string; readonly coordinate: 'original-session' | 'prepared-export';\n    readonly sourceRevision: string; readonly currentRevision: string };\n\nasync function getRecordingWorkshopFiles(recording: StudioRecording, isPrepared: boolean): Promise<RecordingWorkshopFile[]> {\n    if (!recording.workshopMetadata) return [];\n    const sidecar = await createRecordingWorkshopSidecar(recording, isPrepared);\n    if (!sidecar) return [];\n    return [{ filename: `metadata/${isPrepared ? 'prepared' : 'original'}/${recordingFileStem(recording)}-workshop.json`,\n        content: JSON.stringify(sidecar, null, 2), coordinate: isPrepared ? 'prepared-export' : 'original-session',\n        sourceRevision: sidecar.sourceRevision, currentRevision: sidecar.currentRevision }];\n}\n\ntype SaveFilePickerWindow = Window & {\n    showSaveFilePicker?: (options: { suggestedName: string; types: { description: string; accept: Record<string, string[]> }[] }) => Promise<FileSystemFileHandle>;\n};\n\nexport function recordingFileStem(recording: StudioRecording): string {\n    return `${recording.title.normalize('NFKD').replace(/[\\u0300-\\u036f]/g, '').replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]+/g, '-').replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '').slice(0, 70) || 'recording'}-${recording.id.slice(0, 8)}`;\n}\n\nfunction recordingMediaFileExtension(mimeType: string): string {\n    if (mimeType.includes('mp4')) return 'mp4';\n    if (mimeType.includes('ogg')) return 'ogg';\n    return 'webm';\n}\n\n/** Must be invoked before imports/awaits in the export button's gesture. */\nexport function chooseRecordingArchiveDestination(recording: StudioRecording): Promise<FileSystemFileHandle | null> {\n    const picker = (window as SaveFilePickerWindow).showSaveFilePicker;\n    return picker ? picker.call(window, {\n        suggestedName: `${recordingFileStem(recording)}.zip`, types: [{ description: 'ZIP archiv', accept: { 'application/zip': ['.zip'] } }],\n    }) : Promise.resolve(null);\n}\n\nexport function recordingOriginalFilename(recording: StudioRecording, track: RecordingTrack): string {\n    return `${recordingFileStem(recording)}-${recordingSourceNumber(recording, track.id)}-${track.kind}.${recordingMediaFileExtension(track.mimeType)}`;\n}\n\nexport function recordingOriginalPartFilename(recording: StudioRecording, track: RecordingTrack, part: RecordingMediaPart): string {\n    const partIndex = getRecordingMediaParts(track).findIndex((candidate) => candidate.id === part.id);\n    return `${recordingFileStem(recording)}-${recordingSourceNumber(recording, track.id)}-${track.kind}-part-${String(partIndex + 1).padStart(3, '0')}.${recordingMediaFileExtension(part.mimeType)}`;\n}\n\nfunction getPartArchiveFiles(recording: StudioRecording, track: RecordingTrack, prefix: string) {\n    return getRecordingMediaParts(track).map((part, index) => ({ part,\n        file: `originals/${prefix}-part-${String(index + 1).padStart(3, '0')}.${recordingMediaFileExtension(part.mimeType)}` }));\n}\n\n/** Metadata-only manifests report what the capture already checked, without opening any media again. */\nfunction describeRecordedPartIndex(part: RecordingMediaPart): Partial<RecordingArchiveIndexState> {\n    return part.indexStatus ? { status: part.indexStatus, isIndexRebuilt: false } : {};\n}\n\nfunction describeOriginalParts(recording: StudioRecording, track: RecordingTrack) {\n    return getRecordingMediaParts(track).map((part) => ({ partId: part.id, takeId: part.takeId,\n        file: recordingOriginalPartFilename(recording, track, part), sessionStartSeconds: part.sessionStartSeconds,\n        durationSeconds: part.durationSeconds, ...describeRecordedPartIndex(part) }));\n}\n\n/**\n * Hands over one recorded part with a seek index whenever this browser can build one\n *\n * Note: A recorder writes a live container, so an original leaving the studio is a file an editor can play but not\n *       seek in. Copying its packets into an indexed container is the studio's own `ffmpeg -map 0 -c copy` and\n *       changes no media. Where that copy is impossible the recorder's own bytes are handed over unchanged and the\n *       reason is written into the manifest, so an export never waits on an index it cannot produce.\n *\n * @returns what the delivered file says about its index, as the manifest records it\n */\nasync function deliverRecordingOriginal(options: {\n    readonly recording: StudioRecording;\n    readonly part: RecordingMediaPart;\n    readonly signal: AbortSignal;\n    readonly onProgress?: (message: string) => void;\n    /** Without a disk picker a rebuilt container has to be detached into memory, which only small files allow. */\n    readonly maximumBufferedBytes?: number;\n    readonly deliverIndexed: (file: File) => Promise<void>;\n    readonly deliverRecorded: () => Promise<void>;\n}): Promise<RecordingArchiveIndexState> {\n    const media = await readRecordingPart(options.recording.id, options.part, options.signal);\n    // An unanswerable question about the index leaves the export exactly as it was before the index was ever checked.\n    const report = await readRecordingIndexReport(media).catch(() => null);\n    if (!report || report.status !== 'unindexed') {\n        await options.deliverRecorded();\n        return { status: report?.status ?? 'unknown', isIndexRebuilt: false, reason: report?.detail };\n    }\n        await options.deliverRecorded();\n        return { status: report.status, isIndexRebuilt: false, reason: report.detail };\n    }\n    const { withRebuiltRecordingIndex, RecordingIndexRebuildUnavailable } = await import('./recordingStudioReindex');\n    try {\n        return await withRebuiltRecordingIndex({\n            blob: media, format: report.format, signal: options.signal, expectedMedia: options.part.mediaBounds,\n            onProgress: (progress) => options.onProgress?.(`Doplňuji index kontejneru: ${Math.round(progress * 100)} %`),\n            consume: async (file) => {\n                if (options.maximumBufferedBytes !== undefined && file.size > options.maximumBufferedBytes) {\n                    throw new RecordingIndexRebuildUnavailable(`Kontejner s doplněným indexem přesahuje ${Math.round(options.maximumBufferedBytes / 1024 ** 2)} MiB a bez přímého ukládání na disk jej nelze stáhnout. Předává se originál; index doplňte příkazem ${RECORDING_INDEX_REPAIR_COMMAND}.`);\n                }\n                await options.deliverIndexed(file);\n                return { status: 'indexed' as const, isIndexRebuilt: true, reason: report.detail };\n            },\n        });\n    } catch (error) {\n        options.signal.throwIfAborted();\n        if (!(error instanceof RecordingIndexRebuildUnavailable)) throw error;\n        options.onProgress?.(error.message);\n        await options.deliverRecorded();\n        return { status: report.status, isIndexRebuilt: false, reason: error.message };\n    }\n}\n\n/** Storage returns fresh objects; filenames follow the stable source identity. */\nfunction recordingSourceNumber(recording: StudioRecording, sourceId: string): number {\n    const index = recording.tracks.findIndex((track) => track.id === sourceId);\n    if (index < 0) throw new Error('Zdroj nepatří k tomuto záznamu.');\n    return index + 1;\n}\n\nexport function chooseRecordingOriginalDestination(recording: StudioRecording, track: RecordingTrack, part?: RecordingMediaPart): Promise<FileSystemFileHandle | null> {\n    const picker = (window as SaveFilePickerWindow).showSaveFilePicker;\n    return picker ? picker.call(window, { suggestedName: part ? recordingOriginalPartFilename(recording, track, part) : recordingOriginalFilename(recording, track), types: [] }) : Promise.resolve(null);\n}\n\nexport function recordingPreparedFilename(recording: StudioRecording, track: RecordingTrack): string {\n    const extension = track.mimeType.includes('mp4') ? 'mp4' : 'webm';\n    return `${recordingFileStem(recording)}-${recordingSourceNumber(recording, track.id)}-${track.kind}-prepared.${extension}`;\n}\n\nexport function chooseRecordingPreparedDestination(recording: StudioRecording, track: RecordingTrack): Promise<FileSystemFileHandle | null> {\n    const picker = (window as SaveFilePickerWindow).showSaveFilePicker;\n    return picker ? picker.call(window, { suggestedName: recordingPreparedFilename(recording, track), types: [] }) : Promise.resolve(null);\n}\n\n/** One disk-backed output and its explicit sidecar, also available without a whole-session archive. */\nexport async function exportRecordingPrepared(recording: StudioRecording, track: RecordingTrack, destination: FileSystemFileHandle | null, signal: AbortSignal, onProgress: (message: string) => void): Promise<void> {\n    if (!recording.trim) throw new Error('Nejprve vyberte společný interval.');\n    const workshopFiles = await getRecordingWorkshopFiles(recording, true);\n    const part = getRecordingPartForSelection(track, recording.trim);\n    if (!part) throw new Error('Výběr přesahuje více samostatných částí. ZIP obsahuje originály a společný časový předpis; jeden soubor nelze bez dalšího spojování bezpečně připravit.');\n    const partTrack = getRecordingPartTrack(track, part);\n    const { withTrimmedRecordingTrack } = await import('./recordingStudioTrim');\n    await withTrimmedRecordingTrack({ blob: await readRecordingPart(recording.id, part, signal), track: partTrack, trim: recording.trim, signal,\n        onProgress: (progress) => onProgress(`Ořez: ${Math.round(progress * 100)} %`),\n        consume: async (file, _extension, timing) => {\n            const { originalMedia, ...preparedTiming } = timing;\n            const filename = recordingPreparedFilename(recording, track);\n            if (destination) await file.stream().pipeTo(await destination.createWritable(), { signal });\n            else downloadBlobFile({ fileName: filename, blob: await bufferRecordingPreparedDownload(file, signal) });\n            const derivedFiles = getRecordingDerivedFiles(recording, recordingFileStem(recording), true).filter((candidate) => candidate.sourceId === track.id);\n            for (const derivedFile of derivedFiles) downloadBlobFile({ fileName: derivedFile.filename.split('/').pop()!, blob: new Blob([derivedFile.content], { type: derivedFile.type }) });\n            for (const workshopFile of workshopFiles) downloadBlobFile({ fileName: workshopFile.filename.split('/').pop()!, blob: new Blob([workshopFile.content], { type: 'application/json' }) });\n            const manifest = createRecordingArchiveManifest(recording, recording.tracks.map((candidate) => ({\n                ...candidate, originalFile: getRecordingMediaParts(candidate).length === 1 ? recordingOriginalFilename(recording, candidate) : null,\n                originalParts: describeOriginalParts(recording, candidate),\n                trimmedFile: candidate.id === track.id ? filename : null,\n                ...(candidate.id === track.id ? { originalMedia, preparation: { status: 'prepared' as const, processing: 'Video/audio transcoded, timestamp-clipped; video resampled to videoFrameRate when available, otherwise original cadence. No spatial crop. Boundary tolerance 0.05 seconds per component.', preparedTimeZeroSessionSeconds: recording.trim!.startSeconds, ...preparedTiming } } : {}),\n            })), recording.tracks.length === 1, derivedFiles, workshopFiles);\n            downloadBlobFile({ fileName: `${filename}.json`, blob: new Blob([JSON.stringify(manifest, null, 2)], { type: 'application/json' }) });\n        },\n    });\n}\n\n/** A browser download can outlive OPFS cleanup. Detach only bounded small outputs; large ones need a disk stream. */\nexport async function bufferRecordingPreparedDownload(file: Blob, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<Blob> {\n    signal.throwIfAborted();\n    if (file.size > MAXIMUM_BUFFERED_EXPORT_BYTES) {\n        throw new Error('Ořez nad 256 MiB vyžaduje přímé ukládání na disk. V tomto prohlížeči stáhněte originál a časový předpis; velký ořez se do paměti nenačítá.');\n    }\n    const bytes = await file.arrayBuffer();\n    signal.throwIfAborted();\n    return new Blob([bytes], { type: file.type });\n}\n\n/** @returns what the delivered file says about its index, so the studio can report it instead of a bare success. */\nexport async function exportRecordingOriginal(recording: StudioRecording, track: RecordingTrack, destination: FileSystemFileHandle | null, signal: AbortSignal,\n    selectedPart?: RecordingMediaPart, onProgress?: (message: string) => void): Promise<RecordingArchiveIndexState> {\n    signal.throwIfAborted();\n    const workshopFiles = await getRecordingWorkshopFiles(recording, false);\n    const parts = getRecordingMediaParts(track);\n    const part = selectedPart ?? {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_016anDFQAdUqvFToH8gEWetA","type":"tool_result","content":"225\t}\n226\t\n227\t/** Reads only the structural head and tail of a recorded part; media bytes are never decoded or scanned. */\n228\texport async function readRecordingIndexReport(blob: Blob): Promise<RecordingIndexReport> {\n229\t    if (blob.size === 0) return createReport('unknown', 'unknown', 'Část média je prázdná.');\n230\t    const header = await readBlobBytes(blob, 0, Math.min(blob.size, INDEX_HEADER_BYTES));\n231\t    const format = detectRecordingContainerFormat(header);\n232\t    if (format === 'matroska') return readMatroskaIndexReport(header);\n233\t    if (format === 'unknown') return createReport('unknown', 'unknown', 'Kontejner není Matroska ani MP4.');\n234\t    const tail = await readBlobBytes(blob, Math.max(0, blob.size - INDEX_TAIL_BYTES), blob.size);\n235\t    return readIsobmffIndexReport(header, tail, blob.size);\n236\t}\n237\t\n238\t/** A missing index never loses media, so it is announced as a recording which carries on. */\n239\texport function describeRecordingIndexWarning(sourceLabel: string, report: RecordingIndexReport): string {\n240\t    return `Zdroj „${sourceLabel}“ byl zaznamenán bez indexu pro vyhledávání a tento prohlížeč jej neumí dopočítat. ${report.detail} Uložené médium je celé a přehratelné, ale střihač v něm nebude moci přeskakovat; index doplňte příkazem ${RECORDING_INDEX_REPAIR_COMMAND}.`;\n241\t}\n242\t\n243\texport function describeRecordingIndexCheckFailure(sourceLabel: string, error: unknown): string {\n244\t    const reason = error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Kontejner nelze přečíst.';\n245\t    return `Index uzavřené části zdroje „${sourceLabel}“ se nepodařilo zkontrolovat: ${reason} Uložené médium zůstává dostupné; index si ověřte příkazem ${RECORDING_INDEX_REPAIR_COMMAND}.`;\n246\t}\n247\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c3f1314a-cae1-41ec-a96d-862a46014ec8","uuid":"8b2ccb58-1725-451e-9032-975827e11243","timestamp":"2026-09-30T20:24:53.383Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\work\\promptbook-experiments-and-landing-pages\\aldaron\\lib\\recording-studio\\recordingStudioIndex.ts","content":"}\n\n/** Reads only the structural head and tail of a recorded part; media bytes are never decoded or scanned. */\nexport async function readRecordingIndexReport(blob: Blob): Promise<RecordingIndexReport> {\n    if (blob.size === 0) return createReport('unknown', 'unknown', 'Část média je prázdná.');\n    const header = await readBlobBytes(blob, 0, Math.min(blob.size, INDEX_HEADER_BYTES));\n    const format = detectRecordingContainerFormat(header);\n    if (format === 'matroska') return readMatroskaIndexReport(header);\n    if (format === 'unknown') return createReport('unknown', 'unknown', 'Kontejner není Matroska ani MP4.');\n    const tail = await readBlobBytes(blob, Math.max(0, blob.size - INDEX_TAIL_BYTES), blob.size);\n    return readIsobmffIndexReport(header, tail, blob.size);\n}\n\n/** A missing index never loses media, so it is announced as a recording which carries on. */\nexport function describeRecordingIndexWarning(sourceLabel: string, report: RecordingIndexReport): string {\n    return `Zdroj „${sourceLabel}“ byl zaznamenán bez indexu pro vyhledávání a tento prohlížeč jej neumí dopočítat. ${report.detail} Uložené médium je celé a přehratelné, ale střihač v něm nebude moci přeskakovat; index doplňte příkazem ${RECORDING_INDEX_REPAIR_COMMAND}.`;\n}\n\nexport function describeRecordingIndexCheckFailure(sourceLabel: string, error: unknown): string {\n    const reason = error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Kontejner nelze přečíst.';\n    return `Index uzavřené části zdroje „${sourceLabel}“ se nepodařilo zkontrolovat: ${reason} Uložené médium zůstává dostupné; index si ověřte příkazem ${RECORDING_INDEX_REPAIR_COMMAND}.`;\n}\n","numLines":23,"startLine":225,"totalLines":247}}}

(file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c3f1314a-cae1-41ec-a96d-862a46014ec8","uuid":"c391b2ac-7d98-4c35-a07d-332874435ab4","timestamp":"2026-09-30T20:24:58.890Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\work\\promptbook-experiments-and-landing-pages\\aldaron\\lib\\recording-studio\\recordingStudioIndex.ts","oldString":"/** A missing index never loses media, so it is announced as a recording which carries on. */\nexport function describeRecordingIndexWarning(sourceLabel: string, report: RecordingIndexReport): string {","newString":"/** A missing index loses no media, so it is announced as a take which was kept rather than one which failed. */\nexport function describeRecordingIndexWarning(sourceLabel: string, report: RecordingIndexReport): string {","originalFile":"/**\n * What a usable seek index is, and how one recorded container is asked whether it has one\n *\n * Note: `MediaRecorder` writes a live container: the Matroska Segment is left with an unknown size, no Cues are\n *       written and no duration is stored, because the browser is streaming a file whose end it does not know yet.\n *       Such a file plays from the beginning in every player, but an editor cannot seek in it, which is exactly the\n *       state an administrator has been repairing by hand with `ffmpeg -map 0 -c copy`. That repair rewrites the\n *       container around unchanged media, so this module decides once whether a repair is needed at all.\n */\n\n/** The manual repair which always remains available, named in every message about a missing index. */\nexport const RECORDING_INDEX_REPAIR_COMMAND = 'ffmpeg -i zaznam.webm -map 0 -c copy zaznam-fixed.webm';\n\n/** Structural elements live at the head of the container; media bytes are never read to answer this. */\nconst INDEX_HEADER_BYTES = 256 * 1024;\n/** A fragmented MP4 closes with `mfra`/`mfro`, which is the only part of its index stored at the end. */\nconst INDEX_TAIL_BYTES = 64 * 1024;\n/** A live container fills the read window with clusters or fragments; the header is decided long before that. */\nconst MAX_PARSED_ELEMENTS = 4_096;\n\nconst EBML_HEADER_ID = 0x1a45dfa3;\nconst SEGMENT_ID = 0x18538067;\nconst SEEK_HEAD_ID = 0x114d9b74;\nconst SEEK_ENTRY_ID = 0x4dbb;\nconst SEEK_TARGET_ID = 0x53ab;\nconst INFO_ID = 0x1549a966;\nconst DURATION_ID = 0x4489;\nconst CLUSTER_ID = 0x1f43b675;\nconst CUES_ID = 0x1c53bb6b;\nconst CUES_ID_BYTES = [0x1c, 0x53, 0xbb, 0x6b];\n\nexport type RecordingContainerFormat = 'matroska' | 'isobmff' | 'unknown';\n\n/**\n * Whether one recorded container can be seeked in\n *\n * - `indexed`: the container stores both its duration and a seek index.\n * - `unindexed`: it is a live container — playable, but without a usable index.\n * - `unknown`: the container is not one this studio records, or its head is not readable. Never an alarm.\n */\nexport type RecordingIndexStatus = 'indexed' | 'unindexed' | 'unknown';\n\nexport type RecordingIndexReport = {\n    readonly status: RecordingIndexStatus;\n    readonly format: RecordingContainerFormat;\n    readonly isDurationStored: boolean;\n    readonly hasSeekIndex: boolean;\n    /** Names the element which was missing, so a recorded reason and an alert say the same thing. */\n    readonly detail: string;\n};\n\ntype EbmlElement = { readonly id: number; readonly size: number; readonly isUnknownSize: boolean; readonly contentOffset: number };\ntype IsobmffBox = { readonly type: string; readonly size: number; readonly contentOffset: number };\n\nfunction createReport(status: RecordingIndexStatus, format: RecordingContainerFormat, detail: string,\n    measured: { readonly isDurationStored: boolean; readonly hasSeekIndex: boolean } = { isDurationStored: false, hasSeekIndex: false }): RecordingIndexReport {\n    return { status, format, detail, ...measured };\n}\n\nfunction readEbmlId(bytes: Uint8Array, offset: number): { readonly id: number; readonly length: number } | null {\n    const first = bytes[offset];\n    if (first === undefined || first === 0) return null;\n    let length = 1;\n    while (length <= 4 && (first & (0x80 >> (length - 1))) === 0) length += 1;\n    if (length > 4 || offset + length > bytes.length) return null;\n    let id = 0;\n    for (let index = 0; index < length; index += 1) id = id * 0x100 + bytes[offset + index];\n    return { id, length };\n}\n\nfunction readEbmlSize(bytes: Uint8Array, offset: number): { readonly size: number; readonly isUnknownSize: boolean; readonly length: number } | null {\n    const first = bytes[offset];\n    if (first === undefined || first === 0) return null;\n    let length = 1;\n    while (length <= 8 && (first & (0x80 >> (length - 1))) === 0) length += 1;\n    if (length > 8 || offset + length > bytes.length) return null;\n    let size = first & (0xff >> length);\n    let isUnknownSize = size === (0xff >> length);\n    for (let index = 1; index < length; index += 1) {\n        isUnknownSize = isUnknownSize && bytes[offset + index] === 0xff;\n        size = size * 0x100 + bytes[offset + index];\n    }\n    return { size, isUnknownSize, length };\n}\n\nfunction readEbmlElement(bytes: Uint8Array, offset: number): EbmlElement | null {\n    const id = readEbmlId(bytes, offset);\n    if (!id) return null;\n    const size = readEbmlSize(bytes, offset + id.length);\n    // An unknown size fills every value bit, so its number is meaningless rather than out of range.\n    if (!size || (!size.isUnknownSize && !Number.isSafeInteger(size.size))) return null;\n    return { id: id.id, size: size.size, isUnknownSize: size.isUnknownSize, contentOffset: offset + id.length + size.length };\n}\n\n/** Reads the direct children of one element, bounded by both its own size and the read window. */\nfunction readEbmlChildren(bytes: Uint8Array, parent: EbmlElement): EbmlElement[] {\n    const end = parent.isUnknownSize ? bytes.length : Math.min(bytes.length, parent.contentOffset + parent.size);\n    const children: EbmlElement[] = [];\n    let offset = parent.contentOffset;\n    while (offset < end && children.length < MAX_PARSED_ELEMENTS) {\n        const child = readEbmlElement(bytes, offset);\n        if (!child) break;\n        children.push(child);\n        if (child.isUnknownSize) break;\n        offset = child.contentOffset + child.size;\n    }\n    return children;\n}\n\n/** A written index is normally referenced from the SeekHead rather than stored before the clusters. */\nfunction hasMatroskaCuesReference(bytes: Uint8Array, seekHead: EbmlElement): boolean {\n    return readEbmlChildren(bytes, seekHead).some((seek) => seek.id === SEEK_ENTRY_ID &&\n        readEbmlChildren(bytes, seek).some((entry) => entry.id === SEEK_TARGET_ID && entry.size === CUES_ID_BYTES.length &&\n            CUES_ID_BYTES.every((value, index) => bytes[entry.contentOffset + index] === value)));\n}\n\nfunction hasMatroskaStoredDuration(bytes: Uint8Array, info: EbmlElement): boolean {\n    const duration = readEbmlChildren(bytes, info).find((child) => child.id === DURATION_ID);\n    if (!duration || duration.contentOffset + duration.size > bytes.length) return false;\n    const view = new DataView(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset + duration.contentOffset, duration.size);\n    const seconds = duration.size === 4 ? view.getFloat32(0) : duration.size === 8 ? view.getFloat64(0) : 0;\n    return Number.isFinite(seconds) && seconds > 0;\n}\n\nfunction readMatroskaIndexReport(bytes: Uint8Array): RecordingIndexReport {\n    const header = readEbmlElement(bytes, 0);\n    if (!header || header.id !== EBML_HEADER_ID || header.isUnknownSize) return createReport('unknown', 'matroska', 'Hlavičku EBML nelze přečíst.');\n    const segment = readEbmlElement(bytes, header.contentOffset + header.size);\n    if (!segment || segment.id !== SEGMENT_ID) return createReport('unknown', 'matroska', 'Element Segment nelze přečíst.');\n    if (segment.isUnknownSize) {\n        return createReport('unindexed', 'matroska', 'Matroska Segment má neznámou velikost, takže kontejner byl zapsán jako živý proud bez indexu.');\n    }\n    let hasSeekIndex = false;\n    let isDurationStored = false;\n    let isConclusive = false;\n    for (const child of readEbmlChildren(bytes, segment)) {\n        // Every header element precedes the first cluster, so reaching one means nothing further can be found.\n        if (child.id === CLUSTER_ID) { isConclusive = true; break; }\n        if (child.id === CUES_ID) hasSeekIndex = true;\n        if (child.id === SEEK_HEAD_ID) hasSeekIndex = hasSeekIndex || hasMatroskaCuesReference(bytes, child);\n        if (child.id === INFO_ID) isDurationStored = isDurationStored || hasMatroskaStoredDuration(bytes, child);\n        if (child.isUnknownSize) break;\n    }\n    const measured = { hasSeekIndex, isDurationStored };\n    if (hasSeekIndex && isDurationStored) return createReport('indexed', 'matroska', 'Kontejner obsahuje Cues i uloženou délku.', measured);\n    if (!isConclusive) return createReport('unknown', 'matroska', 'Hlavička kontejneru není v přečtené části úplná.', measured);\n    return createReport('unindexed', 'matroska', hasSeekIndex ? 'Matroska neobsahuje uloženou délku.' : 'Matroska neobsahuje element Cues.', measured);\n}\n\nfunction readIsobmffBox(bytes: Uint8Array, offset: number): IsobmffBox | null {\n    if (offset + 8 > bytes.length) return null;\n    const view = new DataView(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset, bytes.byteLength);\n    const declaredSize = view.getUint32(offset);\n    const type = String.fromCharCode(bytes[offset + 4], bytes[offset + 5], bytes[offset + 6], bytes[offset + 7]);\n    if (declaredSize === 1) {\n        if (offset + 16 > bytes.length) return null;\n        const size = Number(view.getBigUint64(offset + 8));\n        return Number.isSafeInteger(size) && size > 16 ? { type, size: size - 16, contentOffset: offset + 16 } : null;\n    }\n    if (declaredSize < 8) return null;\n    return { type, size: declaredSize - 8, contentOffset: offset + 8 };\n}\n\nfunction readIsobmffBoxes(bytes: Uint8Array, start: number, end: number): IsobmffBox[] {\n    const boxes: IsobmffBox[] = [];\n    let offset = start;\n    while (offset < end && boxes.length < MAX_PARSED_ELEMENTS) {\n        const box = readIsobmffBox(bytes, offset);\n        if (!box) break;\n        boxes.push(box);\n        offset = box.contentOffset + box.size;\n    }\n    return boxes;\n}\n\n/** An `mfro` box closes a fragmented file with the byte length of the `mfra` index it belongs to. */\nfunction hasIsobmffFragmentIndexTail(tail: Uint8Array, fileByteLength: number): boolean {\n    if (tail.length < 16) return false;\n    const view = new DataView(tail.buffer, tail.byteOffset, tail.byteLength);\n    const mfroOffset = tail.length - 16;\n    const isMfro = String.fromCharCode(tail[mfroOffset + 4], tail[mfroOffset + 5], tail[mfroOffset + 6], tail[mfroOffset + 7]) === 'mfro';\n    if (!isMfro || view.getUint32(mfroOffset) !== 16) return false;\n    const indexByteLength = view.getUint32(mfroOffset + 12);\n    return indexByteLength >= 16 && indexByteLength <= fileByteLength;\n}\n\nfunction readIsobmffMovieIndex(bytes: Uint8Array, movie: IsobmffBox): { readonly isDurationStored: boolean; readonly isFragmented: boolean } {\n    const children = readIsobmffBoxes(bytes, movie.contentOffset, Math.min(bytes.length, movie.contentOffset + movie.size));\n    const isFragmented = children.some((child) => child.type === 'mvex');\n    const header = children.find((child) => child.type === 'mvhd' && child.contentOffset + child.size <= bytes.length);\n    if (!header) return { isDurationStored: false, isFragmented };\n    const view = new DataView(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset + header.contentOffset, header.size);\n    // Version 0 stores 32-bit times, version 1 the 64-bit ones, which moves the duration behind a longer header.\n    const isLongForm = view.getUint8(0) === 1;\n    if (header.size < (isLongForm ? 32 : 20)) return { isDurationStored: false, isFragmented };\n    const duration = isLongForm ? Number(view.getBigUint64(24)) : view.getUint32(16);\n    return { isDurationStored: Number.isFinite(duration) && duration > 0, isFragmented };\n}\n\nfunction readIsobmffIndexReport(bytes: Uint8Array, tail: Uint8Array, fileByteLength: number): RecordingIndexReport {\n    let hasFragmentIndex = hasIsobmffFragmentIndexTail(tail, fileByteLength);\n    for (const box of readIsobmffBoxes(bytes, 0, bytes.length)) {\n        if (box.type === 'sidx' || box.type === 'mfra') hasFragmentIndex = true;\n        if (box.type !== 'moov' || box.contentOffset + box.size > bytes.length) continue;\n        const { isDurationStored, isFragmented } = readIsobmffMovieIndex(bytes, box);\n        // Sample tables are the index of a plain MP4; a fragmented one needs `mfra` or `sidx` instead.\n        const hasSeekIndex = isFragmented ? hasFragmentIndex : true;\n        const measured = { isDurationStored, hasSeekIndex };\n        if (isDurationStored && hasSeekIndex) return createReport('indexed', 'isobmff', 'Kontejner obsahuje index i uloženou délku.', measured);\n        return createReport('unindexed', 'isobmff', isDurationStored\n            ? 'Fragmentovaný MP4 neobsahuje index mfra ani sidx.'\n            : 'MP4 neobsahuje uloženou délku ve mvhd.', measured);\n    }\n    return createReport('unknown', 'isobmff', 'Box moov není v přečtené části kontejneru.');\n}\n\nfunction detectRecordingContainerFormat(bytes: Uint8Array): RecordingContainerFormat {\n    if (bytes.length >= 4 && bytes[0] === 0x1a && bytes[1] === 0x45 && bytes[2] === 0xdf && bytes[3] === 0xa3) return 'matroska';\n    const box = bytes.length >= 8 ? readIsobmffBox(bytes, 0) : null;\n    return box && ['ftyp', 'styp', 'moov', 'moof'].includes(box.type) ? Export tests cover a rebuilt individual download, the fallback with its\n  reason, and the manifest entries.","originalFile":"# Recording studio seek index: analysis, contract and verification\n\nThe owner reported that studio recordings \"often result in videos with broken index\" and repaired them by hand:\n\n```bash\nfor f in Zaznam-28-9-2026-12-52-35-316ef072-*.webm; do ffmpeg -i \"$f\" -map 0 -c copy \"${f%.webm}-fixed.webm\"; done\n```\n\nThe filename pattern is `recordingOriginalFilename`/`recordingOriginalPartFilename` in\n`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioExport.ts`, so those were **individually downloaded originals**.\n\n## What was actually broken\n\nNothing in the media. `ffmpeg -map 0 -c copy` re-encodes nothing; it only rewrites the container. What was missing\nis the container's seek metadata, and it was missing by design:\n\n- Capture uses `MediaRecorder` (`lib/recording-studio/RecordingStudioCapture.ts`), started with a timeslice so each\n  chunk can be committed atomically to IndexedDB or to a selected directory.\n- A `MediaRecorder` muxes for streaming. Its Matroska `Segment` element carries an **unknown size**, no `Cues`\n  element is written, and `Info/Duration` is absent, because the browser does not know where the file ends while it\n  is still being written. Safari's fragmented MP4 is the same story without an `mfra`/`sidx` index.\n- `readRecordingPart` concatenates the committed chunks verbatim, so an exported original was exactly those live\n  bytes. Players that scan (including this studio's own mediabunny-based preview) cope; editors that rely on the\n  index cannot seek.\n\nSo this was never an intermittent fault — **every** WebM the studio handed out was unseekable, and \"often\" reflects\nwhich downstream tool noticed.\n\n## Why prevention cannot happen inside the recorder\n\n`MediaRecorder` exposes no option to write an index, and its muxer is not replaceable. The only ways to obtain one\nare to write the container ourselves (WebCodecs plus a muxer, which would give up the browser's proven capture path\nand its Safari fallback) or to rewrite the container after the recorder has closed a part.\n\nRewriting the committed media in place was rejected: an 8 Mbit/s screen share is about 1 MB/s, so a one-hour part is\naround 3.6 GB. Doubling that transiently is not acceptable against the browser's ~10 GiB origin estimate, it would\nadd minutes to **Stop**, and for a selected-directory destination it would have to overwrite the immutable fragments\nthat crash recovery depends on. Committed capture bytes therefore stay untouched.\n\n## What the studio does instead\n\n### One home for the question\n\n`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioIndex.ts` is the only place that decides what a usable index is. It has no\ndependencies: it reads at most 256 KiB of the container head plus 64 KiB of its tail through `Blob.slice`, walks the\nEBML or ISOBMFF element headers, and never touches media bytes.\n\n| Status | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| `indexed` | Matroska with `Cues` (or a `SeekHead` entry pointing at them) **and** a stored `Duration`; or MP4 with a non-zero `mvhd` duration and either sample tables or `mfra`/`sidx` |\n| `unindexed` | A live container: an unknown-size `Segment`, missing `Cues`, or a missing/zero duration |\n| `unknown` | Not Matroska or MP4, empty, or a header that does not fit the read window — never raises an alarm |\n\n`RECORDING_INDEX_REPAIR_COMMAND` and the two message builders live there too, so the recorded reason, the alert and\nthe archive README all say the same thing.\n\n### A check immediately after recording, and the alert\n\n`RecordingStudioCapture.verifyPartIndex` runs as each part closes — at a global pause and at Stop, beside the\nexisting `measurePart` — and stores the verdict on `RecordingMediaPart.indexStatus`.\n\nA part without an index is the ordinary outcome, so it is recorded rather than announced; alerting on every take\nwould make the sound and the browser notification worthless. Two outcomes do reach\n`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioAlerts.ts`, both with the new `recording-kept` impact (warning severity, title\n`… je uložený · potřebuje opravu`):\n\n- the container has no index **and** `canRebuildRecordingIndex` reports that this browser could not build one, so\n  only `ffmpeg` will repair it — the message names the exact command;\n- the container could not be checked at all.\n\n`recording-kept` is announced but deliberately **not** written into the take's `errorMessage`: nothing was lost and\nnothing stopped, so a complete take stays `complete` and remains valid for `Donahrát`. Where the work is needed is\nrecorded on the part it concerns. Rebuild support is probed once per MIME type per take.\n\n### The index is written on the way out\n\n`deliverRecordingOriginal` in `recordingStudioExport.ts` is the single rule for handing over recorded media, used by\nboth the individual original download and the ZIP's `originals/` entries. When the stored part is `unindexed` it\ncalls `withRebuiltRecordingIndex` (`recordingStudioReindex.ts`), which is the browser's own `-map 0 -c copy`:\n\n- `Conversion` with `copy: { mode: 'forced', shiftTolerance: 0 }` — a codec that would need transcoding discards its\n  track instead of silently producing different media, and no timestamp may shift, because the take's session\n  mapping was measured against the recorded ones;\n- output through the shared seekable OPFS working file (`recordingStudioTemporaryFile.ts`, extracted from the trim\n  path so trimming and reindexing share one temporary-file and cleanup implementation);\n- the result is accepted only after it reports `indexed` and its bounds match the part's measured `mediaBounds`\n  within 50 ms with the same component count.\n\nAny failure — unsupported codec, missing OPFS, a rebuilt file over the 256 MiB detached-download limit with no disk\npicker, or failed verification — falls back to the recorder's own bytes and records the reason. Each\n`recording.json` `originalParts` entry carries `status`, `isIndexRebuilt` and that `reason`, and `README.txt`\nexplains both cases and names the ffmpeg command.\n\nPrepared (trimmed) files were already written by mediabunny and always carried an index; nothing about them changed.\n\n## Limits\n\n- Committed capture bytes are never rewritten, so a recording restored from IndexedDB or a selected directory is\n  still a live container until it is exported. The studio's own preview does not need the index.\n- A rebuild costs one full read plus one OPFS-sized write per part, which is why the ZIP and the individual download\n  disclose their temporary-space needs exactly as trimming already did.\n- Unknown containers are reported as `unknown` and handed over untouched. That is not a claim that they are fine.\n- Safari's fragmented MP4 path is implemented against the specification and covered by fixtures, but was not\n  verified on a physical Mac; only Chromium/Edge WebM output was exercised end to end.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `npm test -- lib/recording-studio` — the container parser is covered by deterministic byte fixtures built with the\n  shared encoders in `recordingStudioTestUtilities.ts`: a live Segment with both the eight-byte and Chrome's\n  single-byte unknown size, a remuxed container, `Cues` before the clusters, a missing duration, missing `Cues`, a\n  header outgrowing the read window, foreign bytes, a fragmented MP4 with and without a reachable `mfro`, a plain\n  MP4, and a `moov` past the window. Capture tests cover the recorded verdict per part, the alert for a\n  non-rebuildable index, the alert for an uncheckable container, an already indexed container, and a pause closing\n  two parts. Export tests cover a rebuilt individual download, the fallback with its reason, and the manifest.\n- `npm run test-e2e -- tests/e2e/recording-studio.spec.ts` — with real `MediaRecorder` output, the individually\n  downloaded camera original is asserted to be `unindexed` in storage and `indexed` after download, with the same\n  track count and a duration within 50 ms of the recorded media; every one of the five `originals/` entries in the\n  archive is asserted `indexed` and reported as rebuilt in its manifest.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":105,"oldLines":13,"newStart":105,"newLines":15,"lines":[" "," ## Verification"," ","-- `npm test -- lib/recording-studio` — the container parser is covered by deterministic byte fixtures built with the","-  shared encoders in `recordingStudioTestUtilities.ts`: a live Segment with both the eight-byte and Chrome's","-  single-byte unknown size, a remuxed container, `Cues` before the clusters, a missing duration, missing `Cues`, a","-  header outgrowing the read window, foreign bytes, a fragmented MP4 with and without a reachable `mfro`, a plain","-  MP4, and a `moov` past the window. Capture tests cover the recorded verdict per part, the alert for a","-  non-rebuildable index, the alert for an uncheckable container, an already indexed container, and a pause closing","-  two parts. Export tests cover a rebuilt individual download, the fallback with its reason, and the manifest.","+- `npm test -- lib/recording-studio` (156 tests) — the container parser is covered by deterministic byte fixtures","+  built with the shared encoders in `recordingStudioTestUtilities.ts`: a live Segment with both the eight-byte and","+  Chrome's single-byte unknown size, a remuxed container, `Cues` before the clusters, a missing duration, missing","+  `Cues`, a header outgrowing the read window, an empty part, foreign bytes, a fragmented MP4 with and without a","+  reachable `mfro`, a plain MP4, a long-form (64-bit) `mvhd`, an `mvhd` too short to hold its duration, and a `moov`","+  past the window. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_018qhf3rvB9kwmcVgTSwgd7B","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Current preversion\n2\t\n3\t- Recording-studio files no longer leave the studio without a seek index. A browser recorder writes a live container\n4\t  — the Matroska `Segment` keeps an unknown size, no `Cues` are written and no duration is stored — so every original\n5\t  played from the beginning but could not be seeked in, which is what the manual\n6\t  `ffmpeg -i … -map 0 -c copy …` repair was fixing. The studio now decides in one place what a usable index is, from\n7\t  a bounded read of the container's head and tail rather than from its media, and checks every part the moment it\n8\t  closes, at a global pause as well as at Stop. The verdict stays on that part, and both the individual\n9\t  **Stáhnout originál** and the originals inside a ZIP are handed over inside a proper indexed container, rebuilt by\n10\t  forced packet copy through the temporary working file trimming already used: not one packet is re-encoded, no\n11\t  timestamp is shifted, the result is accepted only when it really is seekable and still covers the measured\n12\t  recorded range, and the committed capture bytes in the browser or the chosen folder are never rewritten. Where no\n13\t  index can be built — an unsupported codec, no working storage, a rebuilt file too large to download without a disk\n14\t  picker, or a result which fails that check — the recorder's own bytes are handed over unchanged and the reason is\n15\t  written into `recording.json` beside each part's index status and explained in the archive `README.txt`. An index\n16\t  which cannot be checked at all, or which this browser could never rebuild, is announced through the existing alert\n17\t  channel with the exact `ffmpeg` command, so the administrator hears it while they are still in the room; because\n18\t  nothing was lost and nothing stopped, such a take stays complete and remains available for **Donahrát**. Trimmed\n19\t  files always carried an index and are unchanged. Analysis, the contract and its limits are in\n20\t  `docs/recording-studio-seek-index.md`.\n21\t\n22\t- A recording-studio failure now keeps recording whatever it can and always says so out loud. Losing a camera, a"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c3f1314a-cae1-41ec-a96d-862a46014ec8","uuid":"79291cf3-cf2b-46a7-8d76-f51828b53820","timestamp":"2026-09-30T20:26:52.064Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\work\\promptbook-experiments-and-landing-pages\\aldaron\\changelog\\_current-preversion.md","content":"# Current preversion\n\n- Recording-studio files no longer leave the studio without a seek index. A browser recorder writes a live container\n  — the Matroska `Segment` keeps an unknown size, no `Cues` are written and no duration is stored — so every original\n  played from the beginning but could not be seeked in, which is what the manual\n  `ffmpeg -i … -map 0 -c copy …` repair was fixing. The studio now decides in one place what a usable index is, from\n  a bounded read of the container's head and tail rather than from its media, and checks every part the moment it\n  closes, at a global pause as well as at Stop. The verdict stays on that part, and both the individual\n  **Stáhnout originál** and the originals inside a ZIP are handed over inside a proper indexed container, rebuilt by\n  forced packet copy through the temporary working file trimming already used: not one packet is re-encoded, no\n  timestamp is shifted, the result is accepted only when it really is seekable and still covers the measured\n  recorded range, and the committed capture bytes in the browser or the chosen folder are never rewritten. Where no\n  index can be built — an unsupported codec, no working storage, a rebuilt file too large to download without a disk\n  picker, or a result which fails that check — the recorder's own bytes are handed over unchanged and the reason is\n  written into `recording.json` beside each part's index status and explained in the archive `README.txt`. An index\n  which cannot be checked at all, or which this browser could never rebuild, is announced through the existing alert\n  channel with the exact `ffmpeg` command, so the administrator hears it while they are still in the room; because\n  nothing was lost and nothing stopped, such a take stays complete and remains available for **Donahrát**. Trimmed\n  files always carried an index and are unchanged. Analysis, the contract and its limits are in\n  `docs/recording-studio-seek-index.md`.\n\n- A recording-studio failure now keeps recording whatever it can and always says so out loud. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01AVnRnCMwRUf9ewC5Y4dz5D","type":"tool_result","content":"The file C:\\Users\\me\\work\\promptbook-experiments-and-landing-pages\\aldaron\\changelog\\_current-preversion.md has been updated successfully. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c3f1314a-cae1-41ec-a96d-862a46014ec8","uuid":"e1d6fd1a-4afe-4f60-b763-e200d4eb8405","timestamp":"2026-09-30T20:26:57.462Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\work\\promptbook-experiments-and-landing-pages\\aldaron\\changelog\\_current-preversion.md","oldString":"  **Stáhnout originál** and the originals inside a ZIP are handed over inside a proper indexed container, rebuilt by\n  forced packet copy through the temporary working file trimming already used: not one packet is re-encoded, no","newString":"  **Stáhnout originál** and the originals inside a ZIP are handed over inside a proper indexed container, rebuilt by\n  forced packet copy through the same temporary working file trimming already uses: not one packet is re-encoded, no","originalFile":"# Current preversion\n\n- Recording-studio files no longer leave the studio without a seek index. A browser recorder writes a live container\n  — the Matroska `Segment` keeps an unknown size, no `Cues` are written and no duration is stored — so every original\n  played from the beginning but could not be seeked in, which is what the manual\n  `ffmpeg -i … -map 0 -c copy …` repair was fixing. The studio now decides in one place what a usable index is, from\n  a bounded read of the container's head and tail rather than from its media, and checks every part the moment it\n  closes, at a global pause as well as at Stop. The verdict stays on that part, and both the individual\n  **Stáhnout originál** and the originals inside a ZIP are handed over inside a proper indexed container, rebuilt by\n  forced packet copy through the temporary working file trimming already used: not one packet is re-encoded, no\n  timestamp is shifted, the result is accepted only when it really is seekable and still covers the measured\n  recorded range, and the committed capture bytes in the browser or the chosen folder are never rewritten. Where no\n  index can be built — an unsupported codec, no working storage, a rebuilt file too large to download without a disk\n  picker, or a result which fails that check — the recorder's own bytes are handed over unchanged and the reason is\n  written into `recording.json` beside each part's index status and explained in the archive `README.txt`. An index\n  which cannot be checked at all, or which this browser could never rebuild, is announced through the existing alert\n  channel with the exact `ffmpeg` command, so the administrator hears it while they are still in the room; because\n  nothing was lost and nothing stopped, such a take stays complete and remains available for **Donahrát**. Trimmed\n  files always carried an index and are unchanged. Analysis, the contract and its limits are in\n  `docs/recording-studio-seek-index.md`.\n\n- A recording-studio failure now keeps recording whatever it can and always says so out loud. Losing a camera, a\n  shared window or a microphone stops only that source's track, leaves the rest of the session in it as a gap and\n  lets the other sources record on the same clock; the take itself ends only when nothing is left to record or when\n  the shared storage fails. Every failure — including a stopped, crashed or out-of-space recording — goes through one\n  channel which shows it on the source card and the page, plays an alert sound and posts a browser notification, so\n  an administrator working in the very application being recorded is told without watching the studio tab. Sound and\n  notifications can be turned off separately, are remembered in this browser only, and an explicit **Otestovat\n  výstrahu** button raises a real alert through the real channels before a recording needs them. A take which lost a\n  source is saved as interrupted and names every source it lost.\n\n- Added a shared-clock participant player for hosted workshop recordings with Auto/Editor/Aplikace/Kamera views,\n  camera picture-in-picture, one audible track, event and activity timeline, manual speed and reviewed automatic\n  coding intervals at up to 10×. The existing repository graph highlights the verified anchored SHA at the playhead.\n  Free live viewers receive only the independently remuxed, at-most-two-second segment at the server-delayed playhead; full media byte ranges,\n  past and future segments remain server-gated, while members can seek the complete published recording. The existing\n  YouTube stage, supplementary placement, wrap-up and paid replay offer remain in use. Slow decoders make accelerated\n  navigation wait for a decoded frame rather than desynchronize the tracks. Delivery and publication limits are in\n  `docs/workshop-hosted-player.md`.\n\n- Added private, synchronized hosted recordings for workshop video: direct independent file/sidecar import and a\n  studio **Publish to workshop** action share resumable SHA-256 checked multipart S3 uploads. Schema 5 manifests,\n  prepared timing, codecs, optional metadata and subtitles are verified before an atomic revision switch. Admins get\n  an error report and preview; incomplete files never replace the published revision. Participant requests for the\n  manifest and every media byte range recheck room access and the existing live/free versus paid replay rule. A\n  connected viewer keeps one immutable revision during replacement; abandoned uploads and old revisions have guarded\n  cleanup. Verified unpublished revisions can be resumed for publication after a reload; draft files can be replaced.\n  Existing YouTube settings, teaser, offset and stage choice remain available when switching sources.\n\n- Added browser-local workshop player metadata to the synchronized recording editor: reviewed activity intervals,\n  independent event markers, validated Auto-view scene choices, repository/start SHA and reviewed commit anchors.\n  Speech suggests boundaries only; unclassified gaps stay at 1× and never become automatic coding from silence.\n  Git timestamp proposals require an explicit wall-clock/session calibration and verification against selected branches;\n  confirmed missing SHA references report unavailable, while failed GitHub checks remain unknown. Manual edits survive\n  derived-track regeneration, appended takes and selected-directory reloads; scene validation checks actual video.\n  Manifest schema 5 and original/prepared JSON sidecars use the shared IN/OUT recipe, retain original coordinates and\n  report stale source revisions. This is local metadata for a later player, not published media or visible transcript\n  subtitles. Design and limits are documented in `docs/recording-studio-workshop-metadata.md`.\n\n- Added independent browser-local subtitle and speech-activity revisions to the synchronized recording editor.\n  A finished camera/screen audio stream or standalone microphone is selected for each explicit request; older\n  recordings locally verify actual audio before enabling a source. Czech,\n  English and mixed subtitles reuse the authenticated OpenAI transcription route, while local Silero VAD produces\n  speech, silence, uncertain and unavailable intervals without invented confidence. Overlapping subtitle chunks\n  reconcile matching suggestions while keeping cues recognized by only one chunk. Shared session timing survives\n  offsets, pauses and appended takes. Editable lanes, autosave, undo, progress/cancel/retry and stale-revision labels\n  preserve corrected captions and original media. ZIP and individual source exports include UTF-8 SRT/WebVTT and\n  activity JSON/CSV beside source files, with prepared metadata clipped and rebased to the same IN/OUT as prepared\n  media. Manifest schema 4 distinguishes original and prepared coordinates. Implementation analysis, formats and\n  platform verification limits are in `docs/recording-studio-derived-tracks.md`.\n\n- Extended the shared recording workspace with a persistent live monitor (grid, focused source, pinned source,\n  optional tile hiding/minimizing, preview sound and camera mirroring). Those display settings never change armed\n  capture sources or raw files. A single guarded Pause/Resume closes every source into independently playable,\n  durably checkpointed parts and resumes them on a recorded-content clock without paused wall time. Failed\n  restart, device loss or storage failure interrupts the entire take and retains committed parts. Editing now has\n  **Donahrát do tohoto projektu**: it restores the intended sources, waits for renewed permissions and explicit\n  Start, then appends a new take under the same recording ID. Old media and edits remain; an untouched full range\n  extends while a custom trim remains fixed. ZIP manifests carry take/part identities, timing and real source gaps.\n  Closed parts carry measured encoded bounds and their own camera audio/video settings; shorter tails and older\n  single-file timeline gaps remain explicit. Source reuse for a different new recording remains a separate action. Design and verification evidence are in\n  `docs/recording-studio-monitoring-pause-append.md`.\n\n- Replaced the recording-detail modal with an authenticated preparation workspace at\n  `/admin/recording-studio/<recordingId>`, reusing the studio shell, browser lock, stable IDs and local media.\n  All camera, screen and audio sources now share a zoomable timeline, decoded thumbnails/sparse audio samples,\n  playhead and coordinated play/pause/seek/speed controls. Offset/segment mappings retain gaps and short sources;\n  playback waits for decoder starts, pausing/revealing a source settles its decoded frame, and decoder failures\n  hide stale frames and can be retried. Visual hide/solo and audio mute/solo only affect monitoring,\n  with one audible source initially; every source remains in exports. A common draggable IN/OUT range, precise\n  seconds, undo/reset and protected autosave persist a versioned recipe without changing original bytes. ZIP64\n  and individual-file exports preserve separate sources and embedded audio, include explicit source/session/export\n  timing, record video resampling to the source's nominal cadence, and validate transcoded boundaries within 50 ms\n  per component, including long final frames. Unsupported or discontinuous sources are\n  clearly labelled originals plus recipe. Cancellation/retry preserves originals; export holds the selected edit\n  steady and preserves incomplete trim drafts. Small individual prepared downloads survive temporary-file cleanup;\n  larger ones require direct disk saving instead of an unbounded memory copy. Legacy metadata and directory\n  checkpoints retain their IDs and saved selections, and deep links explain\n  absent local data. Added deterministic timecode/clap, late-session, failure/recovery and external FFmpeg checks;\n  verification details and unavailable macOS/physical-device tests are recorded in `docs/recording-studio-editor.md`.\n\n- Investigated the missing VS Code window reported on another macOS Space. The studio's shared capture path does not\n  enumerate or filter system windows; its optional `displaySurface` value is a type preference, and the browser/OS\n  owns the chooser. Added contextual Spaces guidance beside manual, restored, and historical screen-source selection,\n  plus an authenticated diagnostic which calls plain `getDisplayMedia({ video: true, audio: false })` and records the\n  browser's track events, selected surface, frame callbacks, permission/window-state details, and observed Space-switch\n  continuity. A muted required video track is now visibly unavailable, blocks Start, and interrupts an active take as\n  incomplete with reconnect guidance; an ended display source asks the administrator to select it again. Whole-display\n  sharing stays explicit and warns that other windows and notifications may be recorded. The investigation note\n  includes current standards/browser documentation, dated historical issue context, and a reproduction matrix. The\n  affected Mac/browser versions, system permission state, same-Space/fullscreen/minimized/hidden/monitor results, and\n  frame continuity are still unverified because the physical Mac was unavailable; neither the same-Space trial nor\n  whole-display continuation is claimed as a verified Space-switch workaround. `npm run test-types`, 31 focused unit\n  tests, and seven focused Playwright cases covering the plain probe, screen-source setup, cancellation, muted-source\n  handling, and restored/historic configurations passed. An earlier full 16-case run had one audio/video marker timing\n  assertion pass only on its automatic retry. Display picker/streams are synthetic and do not prove native macOS or\n  physical Windows picker behavior; a tested Space-switch workaround remains outstanding until the affected Mac is\n  reproduced.\n\n- Saved recordings now keep an immutable source-configuration snapshot, with **Použít tuto konfiguraci zdrojů** in\n  their list and editor. Reuse replaces a different browser setup only after confirmation, preserves matching live\n  previews, and routes remaining camera, microphone and display sources through the existing per-source reconnect\n  and readiness flow. Display sharing always requires the browser chooser again; no permission or stream is restored\n  from a saved window name, and reuse never starts recording or edits the original take. Legacy recordings recover\n  only stored track labels and audio details; unknown device identities stay unresolved until the administrator\n  chooses a device. Repeated reuse replaces cards instead of duplicating them.\n\n- Recording source setup now has a versioned schema migration for editable labels, stable logical IDs, order, enabled\n  sources, camera/microphone preferences, sound choices and preferred display-surface hints. Settings stay local to\n  this origin and browser profile, use the existing browser-storage layer, and contain no live streams, permission\n  grants or media. A completed or stopped take no longer releases healthy source previews; the cards say `Náhled\n  aktivní` until the administrator explicitly releases devices or leaves the page. Reload restores preferences but\n  never opens a camera, microphone or display chooser. Each source reconnects from its own action, saved display\n  choices remain hints for a newly opened browser chooser, and a readiness check blocks partial or unavailable takes.\n  The owner can label/reorder sources, disable a source, retry or replace a missing device, remove one source, or\n  explicitly reset the saved setup. Screen selection cancellation retains its setup, and an unavailable selected\n  camera/microphone is never silently replaced. Older source preferences and recording-directory manifests retain\n  their existing values through migration/defaults. All 64 recording-studio unit tests passed. The 12-case browser\n  suite passed in Playwright Chromium 151.0.7922.34 and Microsoft Edge 154.0.4258.37 on Windows 10 Pro 22H2\n  (10.0.19045.7663). Chromium needed its configured fresh-context retry once: the existing synthetic A/V marker\n  check measured 161 ms against its 150 ms bound on the first attempt, then passed on retry; Edge passed all cases\n  first attempt. Both suites closed and reopened the same persistent browser profile and verified that source cards\n  returned without camera, microphone or display capture calls. The added live-preview mute/unmute readiness case\n  also passed individually in both browsers; the full unit suite remained 64/64 after that change. E2E sources and\n  the display chooser are mocked, while MediaRecorder, browser storage, codecs and export remain real, so this\n  verifies browser lifecycle and recording paths rather than physical-device behavior. The reported macOS setup and\n  its native permissions were unavailable here; the owner's exact macOS and browser versions are also unknown.\n  Screen Capture requires renewed user activation and consent for every display request, so each reconnect opens the\n  browser chooser. A saved display-surface type is only a hint and is sent only when `getSupportedConstraints()`\n  reports it.\n\n- New camera sources now default to `Kamera + mikrofon`: choose a camera and a system-default or separate microphone,\n  with an explicit, enabled-by-default `Nahrávat zvuk` option. Camera and microphone are requested together and stored\n  in the same camera media file; the muted preview stays separate from the captured audio. Existing source intent is\n  retained in a versioned browser-local configuration, so a saved video-only choice stays silent and restored sources\n  require an explicit reconnect. The studio shows microphone identity, audio-track presence and a live level meter,\n  preserves a failed sound-enabled setup for retry or an explicit switch to silent video, and clones an already-open\n  matching microphone track safely when it is also configured as a standalone source. Recording metadata and archive\n  manifests now identify embedded camera audio and its selected microphone. Recorder containers and codecs are chosen\n  from combinations accepted by the active browser, with construction-time fallback; standalone audio remains separate.\n  Verification on Windows 10 Pro build 19045 used Playwright Chromium 151.0.7922.34 and Firefox 153.0: the full\n  Chromium recording-studio suite passed 9/9, the camera export contained audible audio, and 240 ms visual/audio\n  markers stayed within 150 ms at the beginning and end in both engines. Automated capture used generated canvas/audio\n  sources in place of physical devices; browser recording, playback, storage and export remained real. The permission UI\n  distinguishes denied, busy, and absent-device retries before an explicit silent-video choice. Chromium reported WebM VP9/Opus, WebM\n  VP8/Opus, generic WebM, and MP4 H.264/AAC candidates; Firefox reported WebM VP8/Opus and generic WebM, so the\n  recorder falls through to the first supported combination. The bundled Playwright WebKit 26.5 on Windows has no\n  `MediaRecorder` and disables the studio; this does not describe native Safari. The reported macOS device/browser\n  setup was not available in this workspace, so its hardware verification remains outstanding.\n\n- Quick-link materials now pass only the trimmed original pasted URL as their body to ordinary material creation,\n  preserving URL spelling, percent encoding, query strings and fragments. Scraped titles, fallback titles and title\n  corrections remain separate. The shared link extractor recognizes complete standalone URLs containing parentheses,\n  brackets or trailing punctuation, so existing tracking, preview cards and QR codes retain the full destination.\n  Previously saved content and the full Markdown editor are unchanged.\n\n- Added a compact email-only request form to the AI ta Krajta homepage. It records a dedicated podcast email-update\n  source and purpose note through the existing `/api/waitlist` contact pipeline, preserves the listener's email for\n  retry on failure, and confirms only after the contact write succeeds. The contacts source filter now includes every\n  source in a merged email history, keeping subscriber requests and collaboration inquiries independently filterable\n  and preserving both in exports. Privacy information links to its canonical Promptbook domain; no campaign sender was\n  added. The same form now appears in the shared podcast footer on the homepage, media kit and branding pages.\n\n- Fixed the AI ta Krajta snake's body wobbling at walls and corners. The simulation now keeps the path through each\n  reflected contact, and shared body strokes follow that path with width and colour tied to travelled distance.\n  The bounded trail stays stable through repeated steering toward an outside pointer and rescales with the canvas.\n  Added deterministic short- and grown-snake coverage for all walls, all corners, repeated rebounds, body joins and\n  responsive resizing.\n\n- Participant materials now show a compact preview card for every rendered link, with a safe page image, title, useful description, and destination domain when available. Each card flips to its existing `PromptbookQrCode` on request; only one QR face stays open in a material list, and its tracked short URL remains the same as the material's Markdown link and open action. Preview metadata loads lazily through an authenticated, visibility-checked room endpoint, which resolves stored shortcode destinations by read-only database lookup and reuses the shared public-page scraper and protected image loader. It neither visits click-tracked redirects nor creates links. Broken or unavailable previews leave the Markdown, open actions, and QR available; shared presentation and video cards use the same interaction.\n\n- Workshop material cards in `/admin/workshops?tab=content` now reorder from a dedicated mouse/touch drag handle or keyboard-accessible move controls and save automatically through the shared admin save queue. Focus stays with the moved material. The numeric order remains available under advanced editor options. A workshop-scoped database transaction locks and reindexes only material IDs, preserves content fields, reconciles concurrent additions and deletions, and broadcasts one room refresh after the complete order is committed.\n\n- Standardized admin editing around the existing shared autosave queue. Workshop materials, settings, polls, member\n  answers, chat corrections, agents, subtitles, contacts, discount codes, short links, and recording trims no longer\n  show a normal Save button; edit forms stay open and report waiting, saving, saved, validation, or request-failure\n  status, with retry only after a failure. Existing-record close actions are labelled clearly and flush before closing.\n  New workshop, material, poll, agent, subtitle, contact, discount-code, quick-link, short-link, and artificial-activity\n  drafts remain local until their explicit create action succeeds. Modified drafts now receive browser unload protection\n  and an explicit discard confirmation on controlled navigation, without turning close into creation. Material and\n  subtitle deletion settle pending edits first; workshop, poll, short-link, and discount-code deletions reject duplicate\n  requests while pending. Creation forms also guard repeated submissions. Validation errors have their own status and\n  do not offer a futile retry; failed requests retain a retry action. Dialog closes flush that editor's autosaves,\n  nested editors and active explicit operations. Discard prompts cover only drafts owned by that dialog and its nested\n  editors, so unrelated drafts do not block a clean close.\n  Workshop and discount-code creation fields lock during submission to preserve the submitted draft. Workshop settings\n  remain inline on their page.\n\n- Workshop settings now choose whether video, presentation, or the connected repository leads the stage. The choice\n  defaults to video, preserves every configured source, and follows the existing countdown, recorded-end, and wrap-up\n  phases. Other accessible sources stay in the shared special-material list exactly once; supplementary recordings\n  continue to use the server's member-aware video projection. Presentation and repository stage views reuse their\n  existing room components, and live settings saves use the existing room refresh broadcast.\n\n- Workshop and community participant administration now shows complete room-level counts for trusted people,\n  untrusted people, and moderators. **Důvěřovat všem** reviews the exact eligible room participants in a confirmation\n  dialog, then grants trust atomically only if that set is unchanged. The existing promotion trigger approves pending\n  submissions while preserving bans and rejected content. A separate, default-off setting can automatically trust only\n  newly created participant identities in that room; turning it off does not revoke earlier trust.\n\n- Workshop material administration now offers **Přidat materiál** for Markdown and **Přidat odkaz** for a quick\n  URL batch. Each valid, distinct URL becomes its own ordinary, editable material with a title from the shared safe\n  page preview or a clear domain fallback; the original query and fragment remain in its tracked link. The dialog\n  reports invalid, repeated and already used destinations, shows publication and access defaults, and creates only\n  on confirmation. Batches append after the largest stored material order, keep per-item failures for retry, and use\n  stable creation IDs to avoid duplicate records after a lost response. The existing short-link and live-room paths\n  handle every new material.\n\n- Isolated Promptbook, AI ta Krajta, and Pavol Hejný's Czech and English sites on the four configured\n  domains and their `www.` aliases within the existing deployment. Unknown, Promptbook-only, foreign-brand,\n  short-link, and unknown file-looking page paths on a branded domain now return that site's localized,\n  fully rendered HTTP 404 at the original URL. Legacy cross-site redirects still work from `ptbk.io`,\n  including podcast children, the `/pavol` language entry, trailing slashes and query strings.\n  Each site's robots file and sitemap describe only its own pages. Shared assets and contact APIs remain\n  available; admin pages stay outside the branded sites and admin APIs retain their authentication.\n  Updated personal language and project links, podcast profile and legal links to canonical destinations,\n  while same-site legal links stay on local and preview hosts. Added browser-level domain, status, metadata,\n  asset, API, and navigation coverage.\n\n- Configured the independently branded sites for their own canonical domains: AI ta Krajta now lives at\n  `https://ai-ta-krajta.cz/`, while Pavol Hejný's Czech and English pages live at\n  `https://pavolhejny.cz/` and `https://pavolhejny.com/`. One shared domain-route map rewrites those concise domain\n  roots to the existing app routes, permanently redirects the former `ptbk.io` paths (including podcast subpages),\n  preserves query strings, and keeps the custom domains' metadata, structured-data links, social cards, and sitemap\n  URLs canonical. Each branded site answers on both its bare apex and its `www.` alias, so a visitor who types\n  `www.ai-ta-krajta.cz`, `www.pavolhejny.cz`, or `www.pavolhejny.com` reaches the branded page instead of being\n  dropped onto the Promptbook homepage; `www.` is folded into the apex in one shared place for the primary and every\n  branded host alike. Shared build output, APIs and static files resolve on the branded host.\n\n- Added per-host episode-appearance factors to the `/ai-ta-krajta` roster draw. Hosts retain the ordinary 1×\n  contribution from their episode appearances, while Katka Fajmanová receives 1.7×, Tomáš Mikolov 5×, and Pavol Hejný\n  0.8× before weighted ordering.\n  The shared calculation affects both the hydration-safe initial order and each visitor's fresh randomized draw.\n\n- Added `Dneska` and `Zítra` event badges ahead of `Tento týden`, based on Prague calendar dates. Shared cards,\n  calendars, landing-page term choices, and the admin picker use the same phases and theme-aware colours. Terms\n  still switch to `Probíhá` at their start and remain eligible for waiting-room choices and follow-up recommendations.\n\n- Added the **Titulky** tab at `/admin/workshops?tab=subtitles` with private Czech, English and mixed-language tracks.\n  Admins can fetch available YouTube captions, generate timed subtitles from an uploaded video/audio recording,\n  import or edit SRT/WebVTT, and download either format. Long recordings are decoded in the browser and transcribed\n  in bounded audio chunks using the existing private OpenAI key; generated drafts are reviewed before explicit creation.\n  Existing tracks autosave through the shared editor, keep original-video timing and source information, and remain\n  separate from participant responses. Added a private subtitle-table migration and documented setup and limitations.\n\n- Workshop project previews on `/cs/komunita` and `/cs/online-workshop/participant` now share the first deployment's\n  image, title, description and address. Missing metadata or broken images retain the application's identity instead\n  of a generic GitHub preview; projects without a deployment keep the repository fallback. The participant preview\n  opens the deployed app alongside the existing repository and deployment links, and loads independently of chat and\n  commits. Late responses from previously selected rooms or projects are discarded; community cards still open the workshop.\n\n- Redesigned the workshop wrap-up PDF for sharing and A4 printing with the Promptbook logo, locally embedded\n  Inter/Outfit fonts, a light room palette, numbered sections and running headers/footers. It now includes a QR code\n  and readable ad hoc short link back to the workshop room, a project preview with all deployment links, and a\n  paginated vector Git graph using the same branch selection, commit bounds and lane layout as the materials panel.\n  Export preparation remains authenticated and uses the existing material-access projection; private room data is\n  excluded. External preview/history failures retain the recap and project links, and longer histories are labelled\n  with a link to continue in the room. No document is stored or workshop database field added.\n\n- Added `/admin/recording-studio` to the shared admin menu and dashboard. Multiple cameras, screen shares (with\n  available shared audio), and optional separate microphones start and stop together, with per-track sizes,\n  elapsed time, and an estimate of remaining browser storage time. Recording chunks persist locally in IndexedDB;\n  a source failure or storage limit stops the whole take, interrupted takes can be recovered, and a browser-wide\n  lock prevents another studio tab from changing an active recording. Saved recordings have shared autosaved\n  trimming and previews, explicit deletion, and ZIP64 downloads containing untouched source files and timing\n  metadata, optionally with separately trimmed copies for the editor. Large archives stream to disk where supported;\n  trimming runs locally using browser codecs and temporary files. Admin navigation waits for active recording and\n  export; reopening the studio waits for its previous instance to release local storage. No recording is uploaded\n  to the server.\n\n- Replaced inline admin creation and editing with shared, accessible popup dialogs across contacts, short links,\n  discount codes, workshop/community settings, materials, polls and member answers, chat corrections, Book agents,\n  artificial activity, and custom chart metrics. Lists now show summaries with explicit New/Edit actions; contact\n  notes and contacted status use the same contact editor. Dialogs contain request errors, keep long forms scrollable\n  on smaller screens, restore keyboard focus, and wait for autosave before closing while retaining invalid or failed drafts.\n\n- Added shared autosaving throughout `/admin` for existing workshop/community settings, materials, polls and answers,\n  chat corrections, Book agents, contacts, discount codes, and short links. Edits are debounced and saved in order;\n  background refreshes and older responses preserve newer typing. Pending or failed edits trigger the browser's\n  close/reload warning, while admin links, editor switches, and sign-out wait for saving. Validation and request\n  errors retain the draft with retry controls; new records and destructive actions keep their explicit buttons.\n  Immediate admin writes also protect the window while their requests are in progress.\n  Newer edits continue saving if an earlier request fails, incomplete discount dates stay protected, and contact\n  refreshes retain local changes. Unlocking materials uses their current draft; repeated poll saves preserve the\n  generated IDs and votes of newly added choices.\n\n- Added **Nasadit na Vercel** to project settings in `/admin/workshops` when a GitHub repository has no deployment URL.\n  The authenticated server integration imports the original repository, reuses one Vercel project per repository,\n  and deploys its production branch with future Git pushes connected. Administration shows progress and errors,\n  supports resuming status checks, and fills in the assigned production URL only after a successful build. The existing\n  settings save, validation, room links and previews handle the result; manual URLs and changed projects are preserved.\n  Documented private `VERCEL_TOKEN` / optional `VERCEL_TEAM_ID` setup; no database migration is needed.\n\n- Added independent starting and ending commit IDs to workshop project settings in `/admin/workshops`, with commit\n  message, author and date previews and separate date-based autofill buttons. The participant project graph opens on\n  the inclusive range and highlights it, with expansion and pagination for history outside it. Missing bounds leave\n  their respective side open.
