request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result);\n1564\t        });\n1565\t        const chunks = await new Promise<number>((resolve) => { const request = database.transaction('chunks').objectStore('chunks').count(); request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result); });\n1566\t        database.close();\n1567\t        return { recording: recordings[0], chunks };\n1568\t    });\n1569\t    expect(metadata.chunks).toBe(0);\n1570\t    expect(metadata.recording.tracks.every((track) => track.byteLength > 0)).toBe(true);\n1571\t    const download = page.waitForEvent('download');\n1572\t    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Originály ZIP', exact: true }).click();\n1573\t    const files = await readArchive((await (await download).path())!);\n1574\t    for (const [name, bytes] of Array.from(files)) {\n1575\t        if (!name.startsWith('originals/')) continue;\n1576\t        const input = new Input({ formats: ALL_FORMATS, source: new BufferSource(bytes) });\n1577\t        try { expect(await input.canRead()).toBe(true); OPFS here replaces only the OS picker; this does NOT test quota bypass.\n        value: async () => (await navigator.storage.getDirectory()).getDirectoryHandle('studio-directory-test', { create: true }),\n    }));\n    await openStudio(page, baseURL);\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Vybrat složku pro nahrávání' }).click();\n    await expect(page.getByRole('region', { name: 'Úložiště záznamu' })).toContainText('Složka studio-directory-test');\n    await addSource(page, 'camera'); await addSource(page, 'screen'); await addSource(page, 'microphone');\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Nahrávat připravené zdroje', exact: true }).click();\n    await expect(page.getByTestId('recording-committed-bytes')).not.toHaveText('0 B');\n    // Origin metadata is a cache for this backend: it must not roll back closed directory checkpoints.\n    await page.evaluate(() => {\n        const originalPut = IDBObjectStore.prototype.put;\n        IDBObjectStore.prototype.put = function (value, key) {\n            const request = key === undefined ? originalPut.call(this, value) : originalPut.call(this, value, key);\n            if (this.name === 'recordings') this.transaction.abort();\n            return request;\n        };\n    });\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Zastavit všechny stopy', exact: true }).click();\n    await expect(page.getByText('Uloženo', { exact: true })).toBeVisible();\n    await page.reload();\n    await expect(page.getByText('Uloženo', { exact: true })).toBeVisible();\n    const metadata = await page.evaluate(async () => {\n        const database = await new Promise<IDBDatabase>((resolve) => { const request = indexedDB.open('promptbook-recording-studio'); request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result); });\n        const recordings = await new Promise<import('@/lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioTypes').StudioRecording[]>((resolve) => {\n            const request = database.transaction('recordings').objectStore('recordings').getAll(); request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result);\n        });\n        const chunks = await new Promise<number>((resolve) => { const request = database.transaction('chunks').objectStore('chunks').count(); request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result); });\n        database.close();\n        return { recording: recordings[0], chunks };\n    });\n    expect(metadata.chunks).toBe(0);\n    expect(metadata.recording.tracks.every((track) => track.byteLength > 0)).toBe(true);\n    const download = page.waitForEvent('download');\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Originály ZIP', exact: true }).click();\n    const files = await readArchive((await (await download).path())!);\n    for (const [name, bytes] of Array.from(files)) {\n        if (!name.startsWith('originals/')) continue;\n        const input = new Input({ formats: ALL_FORMATS, source: new BufferSource(bytes) });\n        try { expect(await input.canRead()).toBe(true); expect(await input.computeDuration()).toBeGreaterThan(3); }\n        finally { input.dispose(); }\n    }\n    await page.evaluate(async (recordingId) => {\n        const parent = await (await navigator.storage.getDirectory()).getDirectoryHandle('studio-directory-test');\n        const directory = await parent.getDirectoryHandle(`promptbook-recording-${recordingId}`);\n        Object.defineProperty(window, 'showDirectoryPicker', { configurable: true, value: async () => directory });\n        const database = await new Promise<IDBDatabase>((resolve) => { const request = indexedDB.open('promptbook-recording-studio'); request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result); });\n        await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {\n            const transaction = database.transaction(['recordings', 'directories'], 'readwrite');\n            transaction.objectStore('recordings').clear(); transaction.objectStore('directories').clear();\n            transaction.oncomplete = () => resolve(); transaction.onabort = () => reject(transaction.error);\n        });\n        database.close();\n    }, metadata.recording.id);\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Obnovit záznam ze složky' }).click();\n    await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Obnovit záznam ze složky' })).toBeEnabled();\n    await page.reload();\n    await expect(page.getByText('Uloženo', { exact: true })).toHaveCount(1);\n\n    // A separate visit with no cached handle must recover even if both destinations refuse further writes.\n    await page.evaluate(async () => {\n        const database = await new Promise<IDBDatabase>((resolve) => { const request = indexedDB.open('promptbook-recording-studio'); request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result); });\n        await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {\n            const transaction = database.transaction(['recordings', 'directories'], 'readwrite');\n            transaction.objectStore('recordings').clear(); transaction.objectStore('directories').clear();\n            transaction.oncomplete = () => resolve();\n        });\n        database.close();\n    });\n    await page.reload();\n    await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Obnovit záznam ze složky' })).toBeEnabled();\n    await page.evaluate(async (recordingId) => {\n        const parent = await (await navigator.storage.getDirectory()).getDirectoryHandle('studio-directory-test');\n        const directory = await parent.getDirectoryHandle(`promptbook-recording-${recordingId}`);\n        Object.defineProperty(window, 'showDirectoryPicker', { configurable: true, value: async () => directory });\n        const originalPut = IDBObjectStore.prototype.put;\n        IDBObjectStore.prototype.put = function (value, key) {\n            const request = key === undefined ? originalPut.call(this, value) : originalPut.call(this, value, key);\n            this.transaction.abort();\n            return request;\n        };\n        FileSystemFileHandle.prototype.createWritable = async () => { throw new DOMException('Simulated full disk', 'QuotaExceededError'); };\n    }, metadata.recording.id);\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Obnovit záznam ze složky' }).click();\n    await expect(page.getByText('Uloženo', { exact: true })).toHaveCount(1);\n    const recoveredDownload = page.waitForEvent('download');\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Stáhnout originál 1', exact: true }).click();\n    const firstOriginal = Array.from(files.keys()).find((name) => name.startsWith('originals/01-camera'));\n    expect(firstOriginal).toBeDefined();\n    expect(await readFile((await (await recoveredDownload).path())!)).toEqual(Buffer.from(files.get(firstOriginal!)!));\n});\n\ntest('keeps committed multi-source data after a real IndexedDB transaction abort and offers recovery', async ({ page, baseURL }) => {\n    await openStudio(page, baseURL);\n    await addSource(page, 'camera'); await addSource(page, 'screen');\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Nahrávat připravené zdroje', exact: true }).click();\n    await expect(page.getByTestId('recording-bitrate')).toContainText('/s');","numLines":100,"startLine":1535,"totalLines":1655}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01LTXgnxLSE7FaqPLiU4fBRo","type":"tool_result","content":"1\tconst EXPORT_TEMPORARY_DIRECTORY = 'promptbook-recording-studio-exports';\n2\t\n3\t/** One seekable disk-backed working file, as both trimming and index rebuilding need it. */\n4\texport type RecordingTemporaryFile = {\n5\t    readonly writable: FileSystemWritableFileStream;\n6\t    readonly readFile: () => Promise<File>;\n7\t};\n8\t\n9\texport function isRecordingTemporaryFileSupported(): boolean {\n10\t    return Boolean(navigator.storage?.getDirectory);\n11\t}\n12\t\n13\texport async function clearRecordingExportTemporaryFiles(): Promise<void> {\n14\t    if (!isRecordingTemporaryFileSupported()) return;\n15\t    const root = await navigator.storage.getDirectory();\n16\t    await root.removeEntry(EXPORT_TEMPORARY_DIRECTORY, { recursive: true }).catch((error: unknown) => {\n17\t        if (!(error instanceof DOMException) || error.name !== 'NotFoundError') throw error;\n18\t    });\n19\t}\n20\t\n21\t/**\n22\t * Runs one output-writing step against a temporary file and removes that file afterwards\n23\t *\n24\t * Note: A Matroska or MP4 index can only be written into a seekable target, so neither trimming nor index\n25\t *       rebuilding can stream straight into a download. Holding a whole transcoded or remuxed camera track in\n26\t *       memory is not an option either, which is why both of them borrow the same disk-backed working file.\n27\t */\n28\texport async function withRecordingTemporaryFile<Result>(runWithFile: (target: RecordingTemporaryFile) => Promise<Result>): Promise<Result> {\n29\t    const root = await navigator.storage.getDirectory();\n30\t    const directory = await root.getDirectoryHandle(EXPORT_TEMPORARY_DIRECTORY, { create: true });\n31\t    const filename = crypto.randomUUID();\n32\t    const handle = await directory.getFileHandle(filename, { create: true });\n33\t    const writable = await handle.createWritable();\n34\t    try {\n35\t        return await runWithFile({ writable, readFile: () => handle.getFile() });\n36\t    } finally {\n37\t        await writable.abort().catch(() => undefined);\n38\t        // A leaked working file is collected when the studio is opened again; it must never mask a real failure.\n39\t        await directory.removeEntry(filename).catch(() => undefined);\n40\t    }\n41\t}\n42\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7ad96718-2338-4700-8fb8-d677fd8d796c","uuid":"5e5501ba-3131-404a-bca0-4fca3a9b1cad","timestamp":"2026-09-30T21:03:50.394Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\work\\promptbook-experiments-and-landing-pages\\aldaron\\lib\\recording-studio\\recordingStudioTemporaryFile.ts","content":"const EXPORT_TEMPORARY_DIRECTORY = 'promptbook-recording-studio-exports';\n\n/** One seekable disk-backed working file, as both trimming and index rebuilding need it. */\nexport type RecordingTemporaryFile = {\n    readonly writable: FileSystemWritableFileStream;\n    readonly readFile: () => Promise<File>;\n};\n\nexport function isRecordingTemporaryFileSupported(): boolean {\n    return Boolean(navigator.storage?.getDirectory);\n}\n\nexport async function clearRecordingExportTemporaryFiles(): Promise<void> {\n    if (!isRecordingTemporaryFileSupported()) return;\n    const root = await navigator.storage.getDirectory();\n    await root.removeEntry(EXPORT_TEMPORARY_DIRECTORY, { recursive: true }).catch((error: unknown) => {\n        if (!(error instanceof DOMException) || error.name !== 'NotFoundError') throw error;\n    });\n}\n\n/**\n * Runs one output-writing step against a temporary file and removes that file afterwards\n *\n * Note: A Matroska or MP4 index can only be written into a seekable target, so neither trimming nor index\n *       rebuilding can stream straight into a download. Holding a whole transcoded or remuxed camera track in\n *       memory is not an option either, which is why both of them borrow the same disk-backed working file.\n */\nexport async function withRecordingTemporaryFile<Result>(runWithFile: (target: RecordingTemporaryFile) => Promise<Result>): Promise<Result> {\n    const root = await navigator.storage.getDirectory();\n    const directory = await root.getDirectoryHandle(EXPORT_TEMPORARY_DIRECTORY, { create: true });\n    const filename = crypto.randomUUID();\n    const handle = await directory.getFileHandle(filename, { create: true });\n    const writable = await handle.createWritable();\n    try {\n        return await runWithFile({ writable, readFile: () => handle.getFile() });\n    } finally {\n        await writable.abort().catch(() => undefined);\n        // A leaked working file is collected when the studio is opened again; it must never mask a real failure.\n        await directory.removeEntry(filename).catch(() => undefined);\n    }\n}\n","numLines":42,"startLine":1,"totalLines":42}}}

Browser load can delay its samples\n                // relative to the wall clock, so the visual pulse must follow this signal rather than a timer.\n                audioAnalyser = context.createAnalyser();\n                audioAnalyser.fftSize = 256;\n                context.createMediaStreamSource(destination.stream).connect(audioAnalyser);\n                await context.resume();\n                const elapsedSeconds = (performance.now() - MARKER_TIME_ORIGIN) / 1000;\n                const audioTimeAtOrigin = context.currentTime - elapsedSeconds;\n                const nextMarkerIndex = Math.max(0, Math.ceil(elapsedSeconds / (MARKER_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS / 1000)));\n                for (let markerIndex = nextMarkerIndex; markerIndex < 100; markerIndex += 1) {\n                    const markerTime = audioTimeAtOrigin + markerIndex * MARKER_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS / 1000;\n                    if (markerTime < context.currentTime) continue;\n                    gain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.2, markerTime);\n                    gain.gain.setValueAtTime(0, markerTime + MARKER_DURATION_SECONDS);\n                }\n            }\n            if (isVideo) {\n                const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');\n                canvas.width = 320; canvas.height = 180;\n                const context = canvas.getContext('2d')!;\n                const audioLevelSamples = new Float32Array(256);\n                const draw = () => {\n                    let isMarkerVisible: boolean;\n                    if (audioAnalyser) {\n                        audioAnalyser.getFloatTimeDomainData(audioLevelSamples);\n                        isMarkerVisible = audioLevelSamples.some((sample) => Math.abs(sample) > 0.04);\n                    } else {\n                        isMarkerVisible = (performance.now() - MARKER_TIME_ORIGIN) % MARKER_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS < MARKER_DURATION_SECONDS * 1000;\n                    }\n                    context.fillStyle = isMarkerVisible ? '#fff' : '#102030';\n                    context.fillRect(0, 0, 320, 180);\n                    context.fillStyle = '#fff'; context.font = '24px sans-serif';\n                    context.fillText(String(performance.now()), 20, 90);\n                };\n                draw();\n                const interval = setInterval(draw, 33);\n                const videoTrack = createStream(Boolean(constraints.video), Boolean(constraints.audio));\n            } },\n            getDisplayMedia: { value: (options: DisplayMediaStreamOptions = {}) => {\n                displayRequests.push(options);\n                if (testSettings.displayErrorName) return Promise.reject(new DOMException('Synthetic display capture cancellation', testSettings.displayErrorName));\n                return createStream(true, options.audio !== false).then((stream) => {\n                    const videoTrack = stream.getVideoTracks()[0];\n                    if (testSettings.displayInitiallyMuted) Object.defineProperty(videoTrack, 'muted', { configurable: true, value: true });\n                    return stream;\n                });\n            } },\n {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_017AWegsCCApB5qoticxnZMR","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Recording studio seek index: analysis, contract and verification\n2\t\n3\tThe owner reported that studio recordings \"often result in videos with broken index\" and repaired them by hand:\n4\t\n5\t```bash\n6\tfor f in Zaznam-28-9-2026-12-52-35-316ef072-*.webm; do ffmpeg -i \"$f\" -map 0 -c copy \"${f%.webm}-fixed.webm\"; done\n7\t```\n8\t\n9\tThe filename pattern is `recordingOriginalFilename`/`recordingOriginalPartFilename` in\n10\t`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioExport.ts`, so those were **individually downloaded originals**.\n11\t\n12\t## What was actually broken\n13\t\n14\tNothing in the media. `ffmpeg -map 0 -c copy` re-encodes nothing; it only rewrites the container. What was missing\n15\tis the container's seek metadata, and it was missing by design:\n16\t\n17\t- Capture uses `MediaRecorder` (`lib/recording-studio/RecordingStudioCapture.ts`), started with a timeslice so each\n18\t  chunk can be committed atomically to IndexedDB or to a selected directory.\n19\t- A `MediaRecorder` muxes for streaming. Its Matroska `Segment` element carries an **unknown size**, no `Cues`\n20\t  element is written, and `Info/Duration` is absent, because the browser does not know where the file ends while it\n21\t  is still being written. Safari's fragmented MP4 is the same story without an `mfra`/`sidx` index.\n22\t- `readRecordingPart` concatenates the committed chunks verbatim, so an exported original was exactly those live\n23\t  bytes. Players that scan (including this studio's own mediabunny-based preview) cope; editors that rely on the\n24\t  index cannot seek.\n25\t\n26\tSo this was never an intermittent fault — **every** WebM the studio handed out was unseekable, and \"often\" reflects\n27\twhich downstream tool noticed.\n28\t\n29\t## Why prevention cannot happen inside the recorder\n30\t\n31\t`MediaRecorder` exposes no option to write an index, and its muxer is not replaceable. The only ways to obtain one\n32\tare to write the container ourselves (WebCodecs plus a muxer, which would give up the browser's proven capture path\n33\tand its Safari fallback) or to rewrite the container after the recorder has closed a part.\n34\t\n35\tRewriting the committed media in place was rejected: an 8 Mbit/s screen share is about 1 MB/s, so a one-hour part is\n36\taround 3.6 GB. Doubling that transiently is not acceptable against the browser's ~10 GiB origin estimate, it would\n37\tadd minutes to **Stop**, and for a selected-directory destination it would have to overwrite the immutable fragments\n38\tthat crash recovery depends on. Committed capture bytes therefore stay untouched.\n39\t\n40\t## What the studio does instead\n41\t\n42\t### One home for the question\n43\t\n44\t`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioIndex.ts` is the only place that decides what a usable index is. It has no\n45\tdependencies: it reads at most 256 KiB of the container head plus 64 KiB of its tail through `Blob.slice`, walks the\n46\tEBML or ISOBMFF element headers, and never touches media bytes.\n47\t\n48\t| Status | Meaning |\n49\t| --- | --- |\n50\t| `indexed` | Matroska with `Cues` (or a `SeekHead` entry pointing at them) **and** a stored `Duration`; or MP4 with a non-zero `mvhd` duration and either sample tables or `mfra`/`sidx` |\n51\t| `unindexed` | A live container: an unknown-size `Segment`, missing `Cues`, or a missing/zero duration |\n52\t| `unknown` | Not Matroska or MP4, empty, or a header that does not fit the read window — never raises an alarm |\n53\t\n54\t`RECORDING_INDEX_REPAIR_COMMAND` and the two message builders live there too, so the recorded reason, the alert and\n55\tthe archive README all say the same thing.\n56\t\n57\t### A check immediately after recording, and the alert\n58\t\n59\t`RecordingStudioCapture.verifyPartIndex` runs as each part closes — at a global pause and at Stop, beside the\n60\texisting `measurePart` — and stores the verdict on `RecordingMediaPart.indexStatus`.\n61\t\n62\tA part without an index is the ordinary outcome, so it is recorded rather than announced; alerting on every take\n63\twould make the sound and the browser notification worthless. Two outcomes do reach\n64\t`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioAlerts.ts`, both with the new `recording-kept` impact (warning severity, title\n65\t`… je uložený · potřebuje opravu`):\n66\t\n67\t- the container has no index **and** `canRebuildRecordingIndex` reports that this browser could not build one, so\n68\t  only `ffmpeg` will repair it — the message names the exact command;\n69\t- the container could not be checked at all.\n70\t\n71\t`recording-kept` is announced but deliberately **not** written into the take's `errorMessage`: nothing was lost and\n72\tnothing stopped, so a complete take stays `complete` and remains valid for `Donahrát`. Where the work is needed is\n73\trecorded on the part it concerns. Rebuild support is probed once per MIME type per take.\n74\t\n75\t### The index is written on the way out\n76\t\n77\t`deliverRecordingOriginal` in `recordingStudioExport.ts` is the single rule for handing over recorded media, used by\n78\tboth the individual original download and the ZIP's `originals/` entries. When the stored part is `unindexed` it\n79\tcalls `withRebuiltRecordingIndex` (`recordingStudioReindex.ts`), which is the browser's own `-map 0 -c copy`:\n80\t\n81\t- `Conversion` with `copy: { mode: 'forced', shiftTolerance: 0 }` — a codec that would need transcoding discards its\n82\t  track instead of silently producing different media, and no timestamp may shift, because the take's session\n83\t  mapping was measured against the recorded ones;\n84\t- output through the shared seekable OPFS working file (`recordingStudioTemporaryFile.ts`, extracted from the trim\n85\t  path so trimming and reindexing share one temporary-file and cleanup implementation);\n86\t- the result is accepted only after it reports `indexed` and its bounds match the part's measured `mediaBounds`\n87\t  within 50 ms with the same component count.\n88\t\n89\tAny failure — unsupported codec, missing OPFS, a rebuilt file over the 256 MiB detached-download limit with no disk\n90\tpicker, or failed verification — falls back to the recorder's own bytes and records the reason. Each\n91\t`recording.json` `originalParts` entry carries `status`, `isIndexRebuilt` and that `reason`, and `README.txt`\n92\texplains both cases and names the ffmpeg command.\n93\t\n94\tPrepared (trimmed) files were already written by mediabunny and always carried an index; nothing about them changed.\n95\t\n96\t## Limits\n97\t\n98\t- Committed capture bytes are never rewritten, so a recording restored from IndexedDB or a selected directory is\n99\t  still a live container until it is exported. The studio's own preview does not need the index.\n100\t- A rebuild costs one full read plus one OPFS-sized write per part, which is why the ZIP and the individual download\n101\t  disclose their temporary-space needs exactly as trimming already did.\n102\t- Unknown containers are reported as `unknown` and handed over untouched. That is not a claim that they are fine.\n103\t- Safari's fragmented MP4 path is implemented against the specification and covered by fixtures, but was not\n104\t  verified on a physical Mac; only Chromium/Edge WebM output was exercised end to end.\n105\t\n106\t## Verification\n107\t\n108\t- `npm test -- lib/recording-studio` (156 tests) — the container parser is covered by deterministic byte fixtures\n109\t  built with the shared encoders in `recordingStudioTestUtilities.ts`: a live Segment with both the eight-byte and\n110\t  Chrome's single-byte unknown size, a remuxed container, `Cues` before the clusters, a missing duration, missing\n111\t  `Cues`, a header outgrowing the read window, an empty part, foreign bytes, a fragmented MP4 with and without a\n112\t  reachable `mfro`, a plain MP4, a long-form (64-bit) `mvhd`, an `mvhd` too short to hold its duration, and a `moov`\n113\t  past the window. Capture tests cover the recorded verdict per part, the single storage read shared by measuring and\n114\t  checking, the alert for a non-rebuildable index, the alert for an uncheckable container, an already indexed\n115\t  container, and a pause closing two parts. Export tests cover a rebuilt individual download, the fallback with its\n116\t  reason, and the manifest entries.\n117\t- `npm run test-e2e -- tests/e2e/recording-studio.spec.ts` — with real `MediaRecorder` output, the individually\n118\t  downloaded camera original is asserted to be `unindexed` in storage and `indexed` after download, with the same\n119\t  track count and a duration within 50 ms of the recorded media; every one of the five `originals/` entries in the\n120\t  archive is asserted `indexed` and reported as rebuilt in its manifest.\n121\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7ad96718-2338-4700-8fb8-d677fd8d796c","uuid":"d4c724be-9564-4221-9e23-3db85d2622fb","timestamp":"2026-09-30T21:11:17.722Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\work\\promptbook-experiments-and-landing-pages\\aldaron\\docs\\recording-studio-seek-index.md","content":"# Recording studio seek index: analysis, contract and verification\n\nThe owner reported that studio recordings \"often result in videos with broken index\" and repaired them by hand:\n\n```bash\nfor f in Zaznam-28-9-2026-12-52-35-316ef072-*.webm; do ffmpeg -i \"$f\" -map 0 -c copy \"${f%.webm}-fixed.webm\"; done\n```\n\nThe filename pattern is `recordingOriginalFilename`/`recordingOriginalPartFilename` in\n`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioExport.ts`, so those were **individually downloaded originals**.\n\n## What was actually broken\n\nNothing in the media. `ffmpeg -map 0 -c copy` re-encodes nothing; it only rewrites the container. What was missing\nis the container's seek metadata, and it was missing by design:\n\n- Capture uses `MediaRecorder` (`lib/recording-studio/RecordingStudioCapture.ts`), started with a timeslice so each\n  chunk can be committed atomically to IndexedDB or to a selected directory.\n- A `MediaRecorder` muxes for streaming. Its Matroska `Segment` element carries an **unknown size**, no `Cues`\n  element is written, and `Info/Duration` is absent, because the browser does not know where the file ends while it\n  is still being written. Safari's fragmented MP4 is the same story without an `mfra`/`sidx` index.\n- `readRecordingPart` concatenates the committed chunks verbatim, so an exported original was exactly those live\n  bytes. Players that scan (including this studio's own mediabunny-based preview) cope; editors that rely on the\n  index cannot seek.\n\nSo this was never an intermittent fault — **every** WebM the studio handed out was unseekable, and \"often\" reflects\nwhich downstream tool noticed.\n\n## Why prevention cannot happen inside the recorder\n\n`MediaRecorder` exposes no option to write an index, and its muxer is not replaceable. The only ways to obtain one\nare to write the container ourselves (WebCodecs plus a muxer, which would give up the browser's proven capture path\nand its Safari fallback) or to rewrite the container after the recorder has closed a part.\n\nRewriting the committed media in place was rejected: an 8 Mbit/s screen share is about 1 MB/s, so a one-hour part is\naround 3.6 GB. Doubling that transiently is not acceptable against the browser's ~10 GiB origin estimate, it would\nadd minutes to **Stop**, and for a selected-directory destination it would have to overwrite the immutable fragments\nthat crash recovery depends on. Committed capture bytes therefore stay untouched.\n\n## What the studio does instead\n\n### One home for the question\n\n`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioIndex.ts` is the only place that decides what a usable index is. It has no\ndependencies: it reads at most 256 KiB of the container head plus 64 KiB of its tail through `Blob.slice`, walks the\nEBML or ISOBMFF element headers, and never touches media bytes.\n\n| Status | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| `indexed` | Matroska with `Cues` (or a `SeekHead` entry pointing at them) **and** a stored `Duration`; or MP4 with a non-zero `mvhd` duration and either sample tables or `mfra`/`sidx` |\n| `unindexed` | A live container: an unknown-size `Segment`, missing `Cues`, or a missing/zero duration |\n| `unknown` | Not Matroska or MP4, empty, or a header that does not fit the read window — never raises an alarm |\n\n`RECORDING_INDEX_REPAIR_COMMAND` and the two message builders live there too, so the recorded reason, the alert and\nthe archive README all say the same thing.\n\n### A check immediately after recording, and the alert\n\n`RecordingStudioCapture.verifyPartIndex` runs as each part closes — at a global pause and at Stop, beside the\nexisting `measurePart` — and stores the verdict on `RecordingMediaPart.indexStatus`.\n\nA part without an index is the ordinary outcome, so it is recorded rather than announced; alerting on every take\nwould make the sound and the browser notification worthless. Two outcomes do reach\n`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioAlerts.ts`, both with the new `recording-kept` impact (warning severity, title\n`… je uložený · potřebuje opravu`):\n\n- the container has no index **and** `canRebuildRecordingIndex` reports that this browser could not build one, so\n  only `ffmpeg` will repair it — the message names the exact command;\n- the container could not be checked at all.\n\n`recording-kept` is announced but deliberately **not** written into the take's `errorMessage`: nothing was lost and\nnothing stopped, so a complete take stays `complete` and remains valid for `Donahrát`. Where the work is needed is\nrecorded on the part it concerns. Rebuild support is probed once per MIME type per take.\n\n### The index is written on the way out\n\n`deliverRecordingOriginal` in `recordingStudioExport.ts` is the single rule for handing over recorded media, used by\nboth the individual original download and the ZIP's `originals/` entries. When the stored part is `unindexed` it\ncalls `withRebuiltRecordingIndex` (`recordingStudioReindex.ts`), which is the browser's own `-map 0 -c copy`:\n\n- `Conversion` with `copy: { mode: 'forced', shiftTolerance: 0 }` — a codec that would need transcoding discards its\n  track instead of silently producing different media, and no timestamp may shift, because the take's session\n  mapping was measured against the recorded ones;\n- output through the shared seekable OPFS working file (`recordingStudioTemporaryFile.ts`, extracted from the trim\n  path so trimming and reindexing share one temporary-file and cleanup implementation);\n- the result is accepted only after it reports `indexed` and its bounds match the part's measured `mediaBounds`\n  within 50 ms with the same component count.\n\nAny failure — unsupported codec, missing OPFS, a rebuilt file over the 256 MiB detached-download limit with no disk\npicker, or failed verification — falls back to the recorder's own bytes and records the reason. Each\n`recording.json` `originalParts` entry carries `status`, `isIndexRebuilt` and that `reason`, and `README.txt`\nexplains both cases and names the ffmpeg command.\n\nPrepared (trimmed) files were already written by mediabunny and always carried an index; nothing about them changed.\n\n## Limits\n\n- Committed capture bytes are never rewritten, so a recording restored from IndexedDB or a selected directory is\n  still a live container until it is exported. The studio's own preview does not need the index.\n- A rebuild costs one full read plus one OPFS-sized write per part, which is why the ZIP and the individual download\n  disclose their temporary-space needs exactly as trimming already did.\n- Unknown containers are reported as `unknown` and handed over untouched. That is not a claim that they are fine.\n- Safari's fragmented MP4 path is implemented against the specification and covered by fixtures, but was not\n  verified on a physical Mac; only Chromium/Edge WebM output was exercised end to end.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `npm test -- lib/recording-studio` (156 tests) — the container parser is covered by deterministic byte fixtures\n  built with the shared encoders in `recordingStudioTestUtilities.ts`: a live Segment with both the eight-byte and\n  Chrome's single-byte unknown size, a remuxed container, `Cues` before the clusters, a missing duration, missing\n  `Cues`, a header outgrowing the read window, an empty part, foreign bytes, a fragmented MP4 with and without a\n  reachable `mfro`, a plain MP4, a long-form (64-bit) `mvhd`, an `mvhd` too short to hold its duration, and a `moov`\n  past the window. Capture tests cover the recorded verdict per part, the single storage read shared by measuring and\n  checking, the alert for a non-rebuildable index, the alert for an uncheckable container, an already indexed\n  container, and a pause closing two parts. Export tests cover a rebuilt individual download, the fallback with its\n  reason, and the manifest entries.\n- `npm run test-e2e -- tests/e2e/recording-studio.spec.ts` — with real `MediaRecorder` output, the individually\n  downloaded camera original is asserted to be `unindexed` in storage and `indexed` after download, with the same\n  track count and a duration within 50 ms of the recorded media; every one of the five `originals/` entries in the\n  archive is asserted `indexed` and reported as rebuilt in its manifest.\n","numLines":121,"startLine":1,"totalLines":121}}}

every one of the five `originals/` entries in the\n  archive is asserted `indexed` and reported as rebuilt in its manifest.","newString":"- `npm run test-e2e -- tests/e2e/recording-studio.spec.ts` — against real `MediaRecorder` output rather than\n  fixtures:\n  - every one of the five `originals/` entries in an archive is asserted `indexed`, and its manifest entry is\n    asserted to report `status: 'indexed'` with `isIndexRebuilt: true`;\n  - the individual **Stáhnout originál** download is asserted byte-identical to the archive's entry for the same\n    part, so one recorded part cannot leave the studio as two different containers;\n  - a seeded already-indexed fixture is still handed over byte-identical to what was stored, so a container which\n    needs nothing is not remuxed;\n  - a recording imported read-only from a folder whose writes all fail is asserted to hand over the recorder's own\n    `unindexed` bytes, to say so in its status line, and to still carry the same track count and a duration within\n    50 ms of the indexed copy in the archive.","originalFile":"# Recording studio seek index: analysis, contract and verification\n\nThe owner reported that studio recordings \"often result in videos with broken index\" and repaired them by hand:\n\n```bash\nfor f in Zaznam-28-9-2026-12-52-35-316ef072-*.webm; do ffmpeg -i \"$f\" -map 0 -c copy \"${f%.webm}-fixed.webm\"; done\n```\n\nThe filename pattern is `recordingOriginalFilename`/`recordingOriginalPartFilename` in\n`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioExport.ts`, so those were **individually downloaded originals**.\n\n## What was actually broken\n\nNothing in the media. `ffmpeg -map 0 -c copy` re-encodes nothing; it only rewrites the container. What was missing\nis the container's seek metadata, and it was missing by design:\n\n- Capture uses `MediaRecorder` (`lib/recording-studio/RecordingStudioCapture.ts`), started with a timeslice so each\n  chunk can be committed atomically to IndexedDB or to a selected directory.\n- A `MediaRecorder` muxes for streaming. Its Matroska `Segment` element carries an **unknown size**, no `Cues`\n  element is written, and `Info/Duration` is absent, because the browser does not know where the file ends while it\n  is still being written. Safari's fragmented MP4 is the same story without an `mfra`/`sidx` index.\n- `readRecordingPart` concatenates the committed chunks verbatim, so an exported original was exactly those live\n  bytes. Players that scan (including this studio's own mediabunny-based preview) cope; editors that rely on the\n  index cannot seek.\n\nSo this was never an intermittent fault — **every** WebM the studio handed out was unseekable, and \"often\" reflects\nwhich downstream tool noticed.\n\n## Why prevention cannot happen inside the recorder\n\n`MediaRecorder` exposes no option to write an index, and its muxer is not replaceable. The only ways to obtain one\nare to write the container ourselves (WebCodecs plus a muxer, which would give up the browser's proven capture path\nand its Safari fallback) or to rewrite the container after the recorder has closed a part.\n\nRewriting the committed media in place was rejected: an 8 Mbit/s screen share is about 1 MB/s, so a one-hour part is\naround 3.6 GB. Doubling that transiently is not acceptable against the browser's ~10 GiB origin estimate, it would\nadd minutes to **Stop**, and for a selected-directory destination it would have to overwrite the immutable fragments\nthat crash recovery depends on. Committed capture bytes therefore stay untouched.\n\n## What the studio does instead\n\n### One home for the question\n\n`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioIndex.ts` is the only place that decides what a usable index is. It has no\ndependencies: it reads at most 256 KiB of the container head plus 64 KiB of its tail through `Blob.slice`, walks the\nEBML or ISOBMFF element headers, and never touches media bytes.\n\n| Status | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| `indexed` | Matroska with `Cues` (or a `SeekHead` entry pointing at them) **and** a stored `Duration`; or MP4 with a non-zero `mvhd` duration and either sample tables or `mfra`/`sidx` |\n| `unindexed` | A live container: an unknown-size `Segment`, missing `Cues`, or a missing/zero duration |\n| `unknown` | Not Matroska or MP4, empty, or a header that does not fit the read window — never raises an alarm |\n\n`RECORDING_INDEX_REPAIR_COMMAND` and the two message builders live there too, so the recorded reason, the alert and\nthe archive README all say the same thing.\n\n### A check immediately after recording, and the alert\n\n`RecordingStudioCapture.verifyPartIndex` runs as each part closes — at a global pause and at Stop, beside the\nexisting `measurePart` — and stores the verdict on `RecordingMediaPart.indexStatus`.\n\nA part without an index is the ordinary outcome, so it is recorded rather than announced; alerting on every take\nwould make the sound and the browser notification worthless. Two outcomes do reach\n`lib/recording-studio/recordingStudioAlerts.ts`, both with the new `recording-kept` impact (warning severity, title\n`… je uložený · potřebuje opravu`):\n\n- the container has no index **and** `canRebuildRecordingIndex` reports that this browser could not build one, so\n  only `ffmpeg` will repair it — the message names the exact command;\n- the container could not be checked at all.\n\n`recording-kept` is announced but deliberately **not** written into the take's `errorMessage`: nothing was lost and\nnothing stopped, so a complete take stays `complete` and remains valid for `Donahrát`. Where the work is needed is\nrecorded on the part it concerns. Rebuild support is probed once per MIME type per take.\n\n### The index is written on the way out\n\n`deliverRecordingOriginal` in `recordingStudioExport.ts` is the single rule for handing over recorded media, used by\nboth the individual original download and the ZIP's `originals/` entries. When the stored part is `unindexed` it\ncalls `withRebuiltRecordingIndex` (`recordingStudioReindex.ts`), which is the browser's own `-map 0 -c copy`:\n\n- `Conversion` with `copy: { mode: 'forced', shiftTolerance: 0 }` — a codec that would need transcoding discards its\n  track instead of silently producing different media, and no timestamp may shift, because the take's session\n  mapping was measured against the recorded ones;\n- output through the shared seekable OPFS working file (`recordingStudioTemporaryFile.ts`, extracted from the trim\n  path so trimming and reindexing share one temporary-file and cleanup implementation);\n- the result is accepted only after it reports `indexed` and its bounds match the part's measured `mediaBounds`\n  within 50 ms with the same component count.\n\nAny failure — unsupported codec, missing OPFS, a rebuilt file over the 256 MiB detached-download limit with no disk\npicker, or failed verification — falls back to the recorder's own bytes and records the reason. Each\n`recording.json` `originalParts` entry carries `status`, `isIndexRebuilt` and that `reason`, and `README.txt`\nexplains both cases and names the ffmpeg command.\n\nPrepared (trimmed) files were already written by mediabunny and always carried an index; nothing about them changed.\n\n## Limits\n\n- Committed capture bytes are never rewritten, so a recording restored from IndexedDB or a selected directory is\n  still a live container until it is exported. The studio's own preview does not need the index.\n- A rebuild costs one full read plus one OPFS-sized write per part, which is why the ZIP and the individual download\n  disclose their temporary-space needs exactly as trimming already did.\n- Unknown containers are reported as `unknown` and handed over untouched. That is not a claim that they are fine.\n- Safari's fragmented MP4 path is implemented against the specification and covered by fixtures, but was not\n  verified on a physical Mac; only Chromium/Edge WebM output was exercised end to end.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `npm test -- lib/recording-studio` (156 tests) — the container parser is covered by deterministic byte fixtures\n  built with the shared encoders in `recordingStudioTestUtilities.ts`: a live Segment with both the eight-byte and\n  Chrome's single-byte unknown size, a remuxed container, `Cues` before the clusters, a missing duration, missing\n  `Cues`, a header outgrowing the read window, an empty part, foreign bytes, a fragmented MP4 with and without a\n  reachable `mfro`, a plain MP4, a long-form (64-bit) `mvhd`, an `mvhd` too short to hold its duration, and a `moov`\n  past the window. Capture tests cover the recorded verdict per part, the single storage read shared by measuring and\n  checking, the alert for a non-rebuildable index, the alert for an uncheckable container, an already indexed\n  container, and a pause closing two parts. Export tests cover a rebuilt individual download, the fallback with its\n  reason, and the manifest entries.\n- `npm run test-e2e -- tests/e2e/recording-studio.spec.ts` — with real `MediaRecorder` output, the individually\n  downloaded camera original is asserted to be `unindexed` in storage and `indexed` after download, with the same\n  track count and a duration within 50 ms of the recorded media; every one of the five `originals/` entries in the\n  archive is asserted `indexed` and reported as rebuilt in its manifest.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":114,"oldLines":7,"newStart":114,"newLines":14,"lines":["   checking, the alert for a non-rebuildable index, the alert for an uncheckable container, an already indexed","   container, and a pause closing two parts. Export tests cover a rebuilt individual download, the fallback with its","   reason, and the manifest entries.","-- `npm run test-e2e -- tests/e2e/recording-studio.spec.ts` — with real `MediaRecorder` output, the individually","-  downloaded camera original is asserted to be `unindexed` in storage and `indexed` after download, with the same","-  track count and a duration within 50 ms of the recorded media; every one of the five `originals/` entries in the","-  archive is asserted `indexed` and reported as rebuilt in its manifest.","+- `npm run test-e2e -- tests/e2e/recording-studio.spec.ts` — against real `MediaRecorder` output rather than","+  fixtures:","+  - every one of the five `originals/` entries in an archive is asserted `indexed`, and its manifest entry is","+    asserted to report `status: 'indexed'` with `isIndexRebuilt: true`;","+  - the individual **Stáhnout originál** download is asserted byte-identical to the archive's entry for the same","+    part, so one recorded part cannot leave the studio as two different containers;","+  - a seeded already-indexed fixture is still handed over byte-identical to what was stored, so a container which","+    needs nothing is not remuxed;","+  - a recording imported read-only from a folder whose writes all fail is asserted to hand over the recorder's own","+    `unindexed` bytes, to say so in its status line, and to still carry the same track count and a duration within","+    50 ms of the indexed copy in the archive."]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}

The recording studio's seek-index\nrebuild (`recordingStudioReindex.ts`) relies on this: an e2e test asserts the individual \"Stáhnout originál\" download\nis byte-identical to the same part's `originals/` entry in the ZIP, which only holds because both remuxes of one\nsource blob produce the same bytes.\n\n**How to apply:** when comparing two mediabunny outputs, compare bytes rather than weakening to a duration/track-count\ncheck — but only when both sides used the same output format options and target kind (a `StreamTarget` reserves\nmaximum-width EBML sizes where a seekable target patches compact ones, so those two differ).\n"}}}
